Kura Sushi's same-store sales declined 5.7 percent in Q4, including an 11.5 percent traffic drop. Kura Sushi’s conveyor belts give diners plenty of reasons to keep reaching for another plate, but getting them to sit down for a weekday lunch is proving more difficult. With customer visits falling and its average check reaching $29, the revolving sushi chain is testing a less expensive way through the door. An October pilot offered meal combinations at $9.99 and $11.99, giving Kura an opportunity to compete for lunch occasions that its typical ticket may put out of reach. The discounted meals accounted for 5 percent of orders during the three-day test, even though Kura promoted them only to rewards members. As an additional positive, the lower-priced options did not reduce average spending per customer, prompting Kura to expand the test ahead of a planned nationwide rollout in fiscal Q2 (December 1 through February 28). READ MORE : Kura Sushi Welcomes Profit Growth Amid Volatile Environment Kura Sushi Hits its Stride Thanks to Collaborations, Tech Investments Before introducing the meals nationwide, Kura plans to adjust the offerings to ensure the lower prices don’t hurt its profit margins. It is also developing off-premises value bundles and preparing paid advertising to reach customers who have never visited. “So if somebody only has $12, we want Kura to be a great option. But if they can spend more, we want them to come as well,” said CEO Jimmy Uba. The push follows a fiscal fourth quarter in which same-store sales declined 5.7 percent, including an 11.5 percent traffic drop. Price and mix contributed 5.8 percent, with effective pricing of 4.2 percent. Kura traced much of its traffic weakness to weekday lunches after studying customer feedback in August. The pressure stretched across markets, making the challenge less a regional issue than a question of how the chain fits into consumers’ everyday spending. The company believes it is attracting diners accustomed to paying more for sushi, pointing to sustained gains in sales mix. Winning those customers, however, has not compensated for the loss of other visits. For instance, in Q1 thus far, same-store sales have improved to negative 3.1 percent, but Uba said the change has come from mix, with traffic largely tracking its Q4 performance. Kura is responding by holding off on another price increase. A previous 3.5 percent increase rolled off at the beginning of November, and the chain chose not to replace it. Its pricing decisions can change, but the current plan calls for margin improvement without additional menu pricing. Uba said rising sushi prices across the industry create an opportunity to attract a larger audience. Kura’s challenge is making its affordability more visible without weakening customers’ perception of its ingredients. Value combinations add another traffic tool to a business that has relied on pop-culture collaborations, collectible prizes, and limited-time food offerings to bring guests back. Kura plans eight intellectual property collaborations in fiscal 2027, up from seven last year. Its Yoshi campaign runs through November and December, followed by Hatsune Miku in January and Godzilla in February and March. Four additional collaborations will follow. The company is also increasing its Kura Reserve limited-time offerings from nine to 12. Not every fourth-quarter collaboration met expectations. Kura also saw traffic change when the World Cup began and expected visits to recover after the tournament ended. That rebound did not materialize as anticipated. In terms of development, Kura is switching how it measures expansion. After establishing a presence in 25 states and nearing 100 restaurants, the company is changing from a percentage-based growth target to an annual opening count that can increase gradually. articles.title: TikTok Shop leva marcas do aplicativo para mídia offline em São Paulo no esquenta da Black Friday
articles.titleKo: TikTok Shop leva marcas do aplicativo para mídia offline em São Paulo no esquenta da Black Friday
articles.originalSummary: O TikTok Shop chegou à Black Friday com ações de mídia offline em São Paulo. As marcas que aderiram aos pacotes do “Super Dia da Marca”, dentro da Campanha PI da plataforma, terão exposição em mídia out-of-home da Eletromidia, em locais como elevadores, Metrô e abrigos de ônibus, além de anúncios no aplicativo da Uber. As ofertas incluem ainda descontos de até 70%, cupons de até R$ 200 para usuários, frete grátis e parcelamento em até 12 vezes sem juros, conforme as condições de cada produto. O calendário promocional segue até o início de dezembro, com a etapa 12.12 prevista para o período de 4 a 9 de dezembro. As Campanhas PI são uma das principais ferramentas para impulsionar vendas no TikTok Shop. Voltadas a momentos importantes, como a estreia de uma marca na plataforma, lançamentos de produtos e grandes promoções, elas concentram ações de venda com participação de criadores de conteúdo, transmissões ao vivo e entretenimento. Elas são divididas em três formatos: Super Dia da Marca: reúne influenciadores, entretenimento e comércio eletrônico em uma ação de vendas de grande escala. Lançamentos: voltadas à divulgação de novos produtos, com foco em visibilidade e conversão. Inauguração: marca a entrada de grandes marcas na plataforma, com ações para ampliar o alcance desde a estreia. As ativações do “Super Dia da Marca” integram a campanha de Black Friday do TikTok Shop, que reúne 25 marcas dos segmentos de moda, beleza, tecnologia, casa, higiene, eletrodomésticos, limpeza e alimentação. A campanha segue o modelo de discovery commerce do TikTok Shop, em que os usuários descobrem produtos por meio de vídeos, transmissões ao vivo (LIVEs) e conteúdos de criadores e podem concluir a compra sem sair do aplicativo . Estudo realizado pelo TikTok Shop em parceria com a NielsenIQ mostra que 74% dos consumidores que compram on-line aprovam a integração entre entretenimento e compras. Além disso, 91% consideram as LIVEs úteis para esclarecer dúvidas e conhecer produtos, enquanto 82% avaliam que a plataforma oferece entregas rápidas. articles.titleKo: Jack in the Box’s CFO Steps Down Amid Leadership Changes
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Jack in the Box announced that Dawn Hooper will be stepping down as Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer, effective April 2, 2027. Hooper will continue to serve as CFO until that time and remain as a consultant as necessary throughout 2027 to support a smooth transition of responsibilities. The company has initiated a search for Hooper’s successor with the assistance of a leading executive search firm. “We thank Dawn for her service and dedication to Jack in the Box throughout her more than 25 years with the company,” said Mark King, Executive Chairman and Interim Chief Executive Officer. “Most recently, as Chief Financial Officer, Dawn has helped lead our efforts to reduce debt and optimize the company’s capital structure. We appreciate her ongoing support during this transition and wish her the best in her next chapter.” Additionally, the company has promoted Shannon McKinney from Senior Vice President, Chief Operating Officer, to Executive Vice President, Chief Operating Officer, effective immediately. In this expanded role, McKinney will oversee the company’s supply chain, in addition to his existing operations responsibilities. The company will continue to evolve its new leadership structure designed to support the company’s next chapter under President Taylor Montgomery, who is expected to succeed Mark King as Chief Executive Officer, as previously announced. “Evolving our leadership structure represents an important step in positioning Jack in the Box for long-term success,” said Montgomery. “Expanding Shannon’s operating responsibilities to include supply chain will help us simplify the organization and strengthen execution. The initiatives we are implementing will improve operational performance and building on these efforts will be critical to driving consistent same-store sales growth, margin expansion, and creating lasting value for our franchisees, employees and shareholders.” The post Jack in the Box’s CFO Steps Down Amid Leadership Changes appeared first on QSR Magazine .

The gains for Steak ‘n Shake continued into Q3, with the brand reporting domestic same-store sales growth of 15.5 percent. Building on a year-ago result of 15.6 percent, the brand is 31.1 percent higher on a two-year stack. Steak ‘n Shake’s makeup has shifted over that time. In Q3 2025, the company had 141 corporate stores, 173 “franchise-partner,” and 96 traditional franchises (the partner model is a $10,000 upfront single-store approach introduced in 2018 and outlined here ). Today, there are 123 company-run restaurants, 186 “franchise-partner,” and 88 traditional franchises. Steak ‘n Shake transitioned seven corporate locations to franchise-partner this past quarter and shuttered a net of one. It also closed a net of six traditional franchises. MORE: Steak ‘n Shake is Getting Political as it Keeps Driving Sales Additionally, as of September 30, eight of 123 company-operated venues were closed. Two were expected to reopen and the remaining six sold or leased. Ultimately, Steak ‘n Shake hopes to transition all corporate restaurants to owner-operators. Regarding that franchise-partner definition, which to the point, is becoming a more prevalent mix of Steak ‘n Shake’s overall footprint—now the largest of its three buckets by more than 60 units—saw Q3 same-store sales results even loftier at 19.1 percent. That’s 33.9 percent over two years. According to the brand’s corporate X account, franchise-partner same-store sales are up more than 19 percent so far in Q4 as well, building off 17 percent from last year. It’s been a hot comps run for Steak ‘n Shake. Same-store sales rose 11.9 percent in Q2 and 14 percent across the first half of the year. It began fiscal 2026 with comps of 10 percent and posted its best calendar run in 2025 since 1992 . Q3 revenue was $74.7 million, up from $69.15 million, year-over-year. Over the first nine months of the year, it’s $210.6 million compared to $200.3 million. Central to the brand’s redirect has been a nod toward higher-quality ingredients. Namely, grass-fed beef and tallow instead of seed oils. That reflected in Q3 results as the cost of food at company-owned units was $15.786 million, or 33.6 percent of net sales versus $14.849 million (31.3 percent of net sales), year-over-year. For a nine-months comparison, the numbers were $43.654 million (32.8 percent) and $41.480 million (30.5 percent), respectively. Steak ‘n Shake said the increase was “primarily because of [the company] materially enhancing the quality of its food ingredients.” This effort began in March 2025 when the brand announced a switch to tallow from seed oils (tots included). Grade A Wisconsin butter, A2 whole milk, cane-sugar bottled soft drinks (August), and the elimination of microwaves (February) followed. In September, Steak ‘n Shake added crinkle-cut fries (also cooked in tallow), allowing customers the opportunity to swap for shoestring. Late August, it claimed to be the first major fast-food chain making buns seed oil-free. Starting October 5, Steak ‘n Shake buns became “unapologetically drenched in pure Grade AA Wisconsin butter,” the company said. In June, Steak ‘n Shake progressed to beef from pasture-raised cattle, stating the product would be 100 percent grass-fed and finished, “making us the only American burger joint serving the healthiest kind of beef.” Steak ‘n Shake previously required suppliers to meet a certain list of standards, such as humane treatment of cattle, no added hormones, and no animal by-products in feed, but didn’t require grass-fed. Carl’s Jr. once had an “All-Natural Burger” in 2014–2015 that was grass-fed, free-range beef and marketed as the first such offering at scale. It was later discontinued. articles.title: Senado aprova R$ 22,6 bilhões em crédito para empresas afetadas pelo tarifaço dos EUA
articles.titleKo: Senado aprova R$ 22,6 bilhões em crédito para empresas afetadas pelo tarifaço dos EUA
articles.originalSummary: O Senado aprovou nesta terça-feira, 17, o projeto resultante da Medida Provisória (MP) 1.379/2026, para criar linhas de crédito no total de R$ 22,6 bilhões, com juros subsidiados, para empresas afetadas pela sobretaxação dos Estados Unidos a produtos brasileiros. O texto segue para sanção. A MP tem validade até a quarta-feira, 18. O texto permite a combinação dos recursos da União com recursos próprios do Banco Nacional de Desenvolvimento Econômico e Social (BNDES). Pelo previsto, R$ 13,5 bilhões vêm do Tesouro Nacional e R$ 9,1 bilhões, do BNDES . A proposta reforça o Plano Brasil Soberano, criado para apoiar empresas afetadas por barreiras comerciais internacionais, tarifas e instabilidades geopolíticas. A ampliação dos recursos deve beneficiar exportadores de produtos industriais, agropecuários, florestais, pesqueiros, aquícolas e minerais, além de seus fornecedores. Inicialmente, o BNDES previa dispor de R$ 5 bilhões. Em setembro, no entanto, o banco ampliou sua participação no Plano Brasil Soberano 3 para R$ 9,1 bilhões. Com os recursos adicionais, o orçamento final do plano de apoio passou dos R$ 18,5 bilhões estimados inicialmente para R$ 22,6 bilhões. Do total de recursos, R$ 8,8 bilhões serão destinados a exportadores e fornecedores afetados pela aplicação de tarifas comerciais pelos Estados Unidos. Outros R$ 6,8 bilhões serão destinados aos beneficiários exportadores e seus fornecedores que exportam para países do Golfo Pérsico, região afetada pelo conflito no Oriente Médio. Os R$ 7 bilhões restantes serão distribuídos da seguinte forma: R$ 1 bilhão para empresas atuantes em setores industriais relevantes ao comércio exterior brasileiro; R$ 4 bilhões para empresas atuantes em atividades relacionadas à fabricação de adubos e fertilizantes ou de intermediários para fertilizantes; R$ 2 bilhões para empresas atuantes em atividades industriais e tecnológicas na cadeia de minerais críticos e estratégicos. articles.title: Liv Up cria linha de pratos de baixa caloria para usuários de canetas emagrecedoras
articles.titleKo: Liv Up cria linha de pratos de baixa caloria para usuários de canetas emagrecedoras
articles.originalSummary: A Liv Up lançou kits de refeições de baixa caloria voltados a consumidores que utilizam GLP-1, as chamadas canetas emagrecedors. Com pratos de até 390 calorias por R$ 17,99 por unidade, a novidade reúne opções congeladas e prontas para aquecer. O portfólio inclui opções como almôndegas de frango com arroz de sete grãos e mix de legumes, estrogonofe de frango com arroz de sete grãos e brócolis, frango oriental com arroz, brócolis e abóbora e yakisoba de frango com legumes. A composição pode variar conforme a disponibilidade de estoque em cada região. “O que vemos é que esse consumidor não está simplesmente procurando comer menos. Ele passa a prestar mais atenção na qualidade e na composição do que come”, afirma Victor Santos, CEO e cofundador da Liv Up. O lançamento acompanha a expansão do uso de medicamentos à base de GLP-1 no Brasil e as mudanças de hábitos associadas aos tratamentos. Pesquisa do Instituto Locomotiva aponta que 33% dos domicílios brasileiros tinham ao menos um morador que usa ou já usou canetas emagrecedoras em fevereiro de 2026. Como esses medicamentos reduzem o apetite, a composição nutricional dos alimentos e a escolha de refeições equilibradas ganham atenção. Os dados da empresa também mostram o avanço desse comportamento entre seus clientes. Há um ano, 6% dos consumidores da Liv Up declaravam já ter usado medicamentos à base de GLP-1. O percentual subiu para 8% há seis meses e chegou a 14% atualmente, mais que o dobro do registrado em 12 meses. Marca abre dark store em João Pessoa A Liv Up inaugurou uma dark store em João Pessoa (PB), ampliando sua operação no Nordeste. A foodtech prevê abrir novas unidades em Niterói (RJ) e Blumenau (SC) nos próximos meses e tem como meta alcançar faturamento de R$ 450 milhões em 2026. A empresa também prevê a inauguração de mais quatro centros de distribuição na região. Além de chegar a novos municípios, a companhia planeja ampliar o catálogo de produtos no e-commerce, expandir a atuação no varejo e conquistar clientes B2B com a marca “Generosa”. A linha foi criada para fornecer refeições equilibradas a equipes operacionais de redes de alimentação e franquias. Entre as empresas que utilizam os produtos estão Burger King, Subway e Bob’s. A iniciativa marcou a entrada da Liv Up no segmento de foodservice. PepsiCo is expanding DRIPS by Pepsi, its crafted beverage platform, with the launch of a proprietary syrup lineup and concentrated bases. Introducing DRIPS by Pepsi Signature Mixes, the first standalone syrups innovation from PepsiCo designed for scalability and menu versatility, and Concentrated Bases to simplify beverage creation. DRIPS by Pepsi® Signature Mixes offer flavors developed from two years of consumer learning and in-market feedback, along with proven recipes that operators can easily add to their menus. Giving Restaurant Operators More Ways to Create Each DRIPS by Pepsi Signature Mix combines multiple flavor notes in a single pump with no added sugar, colors, or artificial preservatives. The syrups are the first to be designed exclusively for the crafted beverage category to help operators bring bold creations to life with less complexity behind the counter, making it easier to move at the speed of culture. The innovative syrups are designed to amplify, not compete with, existing beverage formats and flavor profiles, making it easier to create high-value crafted beverages, from dirty sodas and refreshers to flavor-packed twists on classic favorites. The DRIPS by Pepsi platform is also expanding to include concentrated bases, starting with Lipton® Green Tea flavor, with more to come in 2027. The bases are designed to mix with still or sparkling water, giving operators flexibility to create premium refreshers without expensive, space-consuming equipment. The launches build on the momentum of DRIPS by Pepsi, which since 2024 has tested recipes and met the trend through high-traffic pop-ups, activations, and partnerships across the country. Those real-world learnings helped shape the syrup lineup and the handcrafted beverage recipes behind them. The result is a new way for operators to differentiate their menus, meet consumer demand for a premium product, encourage repeat visits, and stay connected to evolving beverage trends. “The future of beverages isn’t just about what goes into the cup. It’s about creating experiences consumers can’t find everywhere else. DRIPS by Pepsi is an end-to-end platform built on consumer insights, trend forecasting, proprietary recipes, operational resources, and marketing tools that help operators of all size and scale bring crafted beverage programs to life. These syrups are the latest extension of that platform, making it easier for restaurant teams to create customized, handcrafted beverages while staying ahead of emerging consumer trends. Our goal is to simplify innovation so operators can focus on delivering memorable experiences and driving growth,” said Scott Finlow, Chief Marketing Officer, PepsiCo Away From Home. The real fun starts when the Signature Mixes meet PepsiCo’s beverage portfolio Whether paired with PEPSI, MOUNTAIN DEW, STARRY, MUG Root Beer or poppi , the DRIPS by Pepsi Signature Mixes can transform beloved brands into something entirely new. Built for everything from dirty sodas and refreshers to emerging energy-forward beverages, the platform gives operators room to experiment, innovate and create one-of-a-kind experiences for consumers with more than 100+ different recipes to choose from. And with countless combinations still unexplored, the next fan favorite may be just one pour away. Five Distinct DRIPS by Pepsi Signature Mixes. Unlimited Possibilities. articles.title: Donatos Partners with Eulerity to Automate Local Marketing Across Every Restaurant
articles.titleKo: Donatos Partners with Eulerity to Automate Local Marketing Across Every Restaurant
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Donatos Pizza today announced a partnership with Eulerity, the AI-powered marketing automation platform built for multi-location brands, to bring its local digital marketing in-house and automate it across every restaurant. The move extends Donatos decades-long commitment to automation from the kitchen to its marketing, replacing fragmented digital media workflows with one automated system that runs paid media across Search, Social, Display, Video and connected TV (CTV). The partnership was unveiled on the main stage at the Donatos Franchise Conference in Columbus, Ohio, where the team outlined how Donatos will run a unified brand strategy while giving each local market the flexibility to compete in its own neighborhood. Automation from the kitchen to local marketing From its first pepperoni machine to today’s robot-assisted pizza kitchen, Donatos has a long history of putting automation to work where machines do the job best. Eulerity takes the same approach to marketing, freeing corporate marketing teams to focus on strategy while the platform handles the operational tasks better managed by systems. Across hundreds of locations, those tasks add up. Teams manage six to ten advertising platforms, data sits in disconnected systems, and agency workflows can delay campaign changes by one to two weeks. With Eulerity, Donatos sees every dollar, every market and every result in one place, and can adjust campaigns the same day. “We’ve always relied on automation to free up our team for higher-value work, and the most important of that work is the guest experience. Marketing is the next step. With Eulerity, our local marketing runs with omnichannel automation in every market, so our people can spend less time managing ad platforms and more time on strategy and on our guests,” Jodie Conrad, Chief Marketing Officer, Donatos Pizza. Putting Donatos’ own data to work Donatos will use its own first-party data to direct local advertising more precisely through three capabilities: First-Party Audience Engagement : Reconnect with existing Donatos guests through personalized marketing that drives loyalty and repeat visits. Intelligent Retargeting : Re-engage consumers who have interacted with Donatos across digital channels, keeping the brand top of mind. Lookalike Audience Expansion : Identify and reach new local customers who share characteristics with Donatos’ most valuable guests. Eulerity layers these signals with neighborhood-level targeting and geofencing, and its geo-location reporting flags coverage gaps so local media can fill them automatically. One brand standard, more working media Eulerity’s campaign blueprints give Donatos a consistent foundation across every location, while each market tailors its media plan to its own objectives and budget. Applied consistently, those local budgets stop acting like hundreds of small, disconnected buys and start behaving like a single national one, unlocking better optimization, pricing and broader reach. “The strongest restaurant brands own their marketing, their data and their results, and that’s exactly what Donatos is doing. Our job is to make that simple. We give corporate one standard to build on and give every Donatos market the tools to win locally,” said Adam Chandler, COO and Co-Founder of Eulerity. With the holidays upon us, Stoney River is more prepared than ever to deliver unforgettable dining experiences. Today’s diners want every night out to feel like an occasion, and Stoney River – the steakhouse known for its hand-cut steaks, fresh seafood and signature house specialties, bringing a fine-dining experience at an accessible price point – has reimagined every plate to deliver just that. The revamped menu lineup arrives at all locations Nov. 12, giving classic favorites a refined twist and adding starters, surf-and-turf pairings and shareable “For the Table” sides. Before anything changed, the team studied the fine-dining and upscale-casual competitive landscape and tested each dish in four restaurants. Only the improvements that would truly wow guests and keep the experience approachable moved forward. The work began, appropriately, with the star of the show: Prime Beef. Certified Angus Beef Prime must clear USDA Prime marbling requirements plus nine additional specifications, and only Black Angus cattle qualify. Stoney River has long sourced from the Midwest, where cold winters keep herds eating more, and chefs can taste the difference. In fact, Certified Angus Beef Prime represents the top 3% of beef, making it a relatively rare offering in restaurants and an obvious choice for a kitchen determined to stand apart. Filet Mignon stands proudly on its own, whether made with Stoney River’s own coffee-cured blend or served as a Center Cut in petite or regular portions. Then there’s the best of both worlds, where tender Filet Medallions meet their match in a crab cake, broiled lobster or Oscar-style crab for a land-and-sea romance meant to be lingered over. From there, attention moved outward. Shrimp got bigger, the catch got better and even the table settings received an upgrade that feels upscale yet approachable. The fryers switched to beef tallow for potatoes, giving the Parmesan Truffle Fries a crisper edge and a deeper, more savory finish. The comprehensive refresh carries through the rest of the meal: Starters: An expanded appetizer lineup includes the Grilled Seafood Platter, Jumbo Shrimp Cocktail and Crab Stuffed Mushrooms. Soups and salads: Four featured salads, including The Wedge, Steak Salad, House Salad and Classic Caesar Salad, served with house-made dressings, alongside French Onion Soup and New England Lobster Bisque. Prime may lead the way, but the rest of the menu stays deliberately balanced and accessible. Prices range from about $19 for a burger, $30 for a pasta and $50 for a steak, with Steak and Biscuits near $25. articles.title: TikTok Shop já é opção de compra para 22% dos consumidores e entra no top 3 do e-commerce
articles.titleKo: TikTok Shop já é opção de compra para 22% dos consumidores e entra no top 3 do e-commerce
articles.originalSummary: O TikTok Shop aparece como a terceira plataforma mais citada por compradores online às vésperas da Black Friday. Na pesquisa da Worldpanel by Numerator, 22% dos entrevistados afirmaram ter comprado pelo aplicativo nos últimos 30 dias. O índice coloca a rede atrás apenas da Shopee , com 79%, e do Mercado Livre, com 41%. A plataforma supera a Shein, citada por 20% dos compradores, e a Amazon, por 16%. Os resultados refletem apenas as respostas dos participantes da pesquisa e não podem ser generalizados para a população brasileira. A pesquisa mostra ainda que os participantes compram em diferentes plataformas. Em média, cada consumidor on-line citou 2,2 plataformas utilizadas nos últimos 30 dias. “Os participantes relataram compras em mais de uma plataforma, mostrando que diferentes empresas fazem parte da rotina de um mesmo consumidor. Nesse grupo, o TikTok Shop aparece entre as três opções mais citadas, ao lado de plataformas já consolidadas no comércio eletrônico”, analisa Daniel Horai, diretor da Worldpanel by Numerator. Compradores frequentes lideram pedidos online O levantamento também mostra a frequência de compras entre os participantes. Dos 1.804 entrevistados que souberam informar quantas compras on-line fizeram nos últimos 30 dias, a média foi de 3,7 no período. Os consumidores que fizeram cinco compras ou mais representaram 28% desse grupo, mas responderam por 55% do total de compras declaradas. O percentual se refere à quantidade de pedidos, não aos valores gastos, e mostra a participação dos compradores mais frequentes no volume registrado pela pesquisa. Chef Melba Wilson, celebrated restaurateur, community leader, and owner of Melba’s Restaurant in Harlem, is once again bringing the community together for her annual Thanksgiving Giveaway on Monday, November 23, continuing her longstanding commitment to supporting local children and families during the holiday season. This year’s initiative will provide approximately 1,000 Thanksgiving turkeys to individuals and families. Taking place at Melba’s Restaurant (300 West 114th Street), this year’s initiative will bring together Bank of America, Timberland, recording artist, fashion designer and entrepreneur FERG, God’s Love We Deliver, and Wollman Rink to help make the holiday season a little brighter for the community. Beginning at 5 p.m., Melba’s will host its annual public Thanksgiving Turkey Giveaway, distributing free turkeys to community members and families until 7 p.m. This year’s turkeys have been generously underwritten by Bank of America, helping Melba’s continue its tradition of giving back to the community it serves. Earlier in the day, Melba and her partners will also host a private holiday distribution for select students from PS 161 and the Wadleigh Secondary School for the Performing & Visual Arts, continuing their collective commitment to supporting local children and families. FERG is also expected to participate in the day’s festivities. “Food is not a luxury, it’s a necessity,” said Melba Wilson. “For way too many families, putting a meal on the table is a daily challenge and the holiday season can make those struggles even more difficult. No family should ever have to worry about where their next meal is coming from, especially during a time of year centered on gratitude, family, and togetherness. I feel that it is our responsibility to show up for our communities in meaningful ways. Through our annual Thanksgiving Turkey Giveaway, we are doing a small part to make sure more families can enjoy a wonderful Thanksgiving meal because at the end of the day, taking care of one another, is what community truly is all about.” “Melba has a wonderful way of bringing people together and reminding us what it means to show up for one another, especially during the holidays,” said Connie Verducci, Market Executive, Bank of America New York City. “We’re grateful to have worked alongside her on so many efforts close to her heart, and proud to once again come together to help make Thanksgiving special for local families.” “Timberland was born in New England, but we were raised in New York City—it’s our second home,” said Nina Flood, global brand president for Timberland. “We are honored to partner with Melba’s to support the young people of Harlem as we head into the holiday season. Because nothing is more powerful than coming together to build strong communities.” “Melba’s unwavering dedication to uplifting the community perfectly aligns with our mission to make ice skating at Wollman Rink an accessible, welcoming activity for everyone, and we are honored to support their vital work during this special time of year,” said Stacy Shuster, VP of Business Development and Community Impact at Wollman Rink. “Harlem is the village I come from and it always feels good to be able to help whenever I can,” said FERG. The annual giveaway reflects Melba’s longstanding dedication to community engagement and addressing food insecurity throughout New York City. Through her restaurant and ongoing community initiatives, Wilson has consistently worked to support families, provide meals for children, and create opportunities to give back to the Harlem neighborhood she calls home. articles.title: La Morocha, First U.S. Concept from Chef David Castro Hussong, Opens in L.A.’s Arts District
articles.titleKo: La Morocha, First U.S. Concept from Chef David Castro Hussong, Opens in L.A.’s Arts District
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . From the group behind award-winning Los Angeles concepts Mírate and Daisy Margarita Bar as well as the recently opened Gilbert Pérez Bar comes La Morocha, the newest addition to the Arts District, opening Thursday, November 19. A reimagined Los Angeles outpost of the original Ensenada restaurant, La Morocha marks the first U.S. concept from acclaimed Chef David Castro Hussong, whose culinary experience spans celebrated destinations including Blue Hill at Stone Barns, Eleven Madison Park, Cala and Valle de Guadalupe’s Fauna, named Best Restaurant in Mexico and recognized on both Latin America’s and The World’s 50 Best Restaurants lists. It also marks Castro Hussong’s first creative collaboration with restaurateur Matt Egan, a leading force in Los Angeles’ contemporary Mexican dining scene, alongside the group’s key collaborators Randy Evans and Brian Kang. Merging the group’s agave-driven approach and Castro Hussong’s deep Baja roots, the restaurant will serve wood-fired Baja comfort food complemented by Mexican-inspired cocktails and a global wine and spirits program. A TASTE OF ENSENADA IN DTLA On the menu at La Morocha is an assortment of approachable and shareable plates, each inspired by the places where Chef Castro Hussong grew up and the foods he enjoys eating at home. While guests can order popular mainstay dishes from the original Ensenada concept, like its famed Chile Relleno tacos with rockfish, capers, costra de queso, and a flour tortilla, most of the menu is exclusive to Los Angeles and tailored to the local palate. The raw bar draws on the fresh seafood Ensenada is known for, including oysters, ceviches, crudos, and a perfectly spicy Aguachile Rojo made with scallops, chiltepin, jicama, and cucumber. Chef Castro Hussong’s answer to Los Angeles’s fusion pizza conversation is the “Picza,” a playful, Spanish-spelled riff on pizza that lands somewhere between a pie and a tostada, with a golden base and generous toppings. Additional highlights from La Morocha’s list of starters, tacos, and large entrees include: Baja Fish Taco with fried rockfish, salsa verde, chipotle aioli, and corn tortilla Ribeye Taco with grilled steak, salsa toreada, and costra de queso on a flour tortilla Pizca de Cangrejo featuring fresh, sweet crab, beurre blanc, chives and lemon Picza de Flor de Calabaza with squash blossoms, pomodoro, and queso Pescado en Adobo with pasilla mixe adobo, black beans, rice, and flour tortillas Eggplant Milanesa with chile morita, pomodoro, and Monterey cheese Rounding out La Morocha’s menu are desserts thoughtfully developed by celebrated pastry chef Maribel Aldaco Silva, Chef Castro Hussong’s wife and the recipient of Latin America’s Best Pastry Chef award in 2023. The menu features Pixtle Cheesecake; Coffee Churro with coffee ganache, vanilla and coffee ice cream;Mexican Cinnamon Macaroon with chocolate cream, chocolate crisp, and plantain ice cream; and a refreshing Mango and Passion Fruit Sorbet finished with coconut granita and coconut flake. COCKTAILS TO COMPLEMENT Led by Bar Manager Marcos Pulido, who trained under Max Reis at Daisy Margarita Bar, La Morocha’s beverage program celebrates vibrant Mediterranean and Baja flavors, focusing on fresh ingredients, wood-fired aromas, and beach sips. Think ingredients like roasted carrots and pineapple, prickly pear, nixtamal corn, hoja santo, and guava. Standouts include the Zona Centro with watermelon, strawberry, guava, aloe, orange licor and tequila; Reina Querida built on prickly pear, canela y jamaica tea, champagne foam, and mezcal; and La Cura with chile y nogave, ginger, lemon, and reposado tequila. SPOTLIGHT ON MEXICAN WINE Curated by sommelier Felicia Chavez, La Morocha’s wine list centers around the diversity of Mexican winemaking, with a focus on Valle de Guadalupe and other notable regions, alongside classic California selections

articles.title: Nestlé lança espelho com IA que analisa saúde para impulsionar venda de suplementos
articles.titleKo: Nestlé lança espelho com IA que analisa saúde para impulsionar venda de suplementos
articles.originalSummary: A Nestlé lançou o Espelho do Bem-Estar, equipamento que faz leitura facial em 30 segundos para apresentar indicadores de saúde e nutrição. A tecnologia estreia em Fortaleza em parceria com a Pague Menos, enquanto uma versão para iPad chega a farmácias de Salvador e São Paulo. Com a iniciativa, a fabricante projeta dobrar as vendas de suplementos proteicos, vitaminas e minerais nas lojas participantes. Por meio de uma câmera integrada, a tecnologia combina visão computacional e Inteligência Artificial para identificar pequenas variações visuais provocadas pela circulação sanguínea em regiões específicas do rosto. O sistema foi desenvolvido com base na análise de imagens faciais de mais de 60 mil pessoas, sob supervisão de profissionais de saúde. O sistema estima parâmetros como frequências cardíaca e respiratória, nível de estresse, equilíbrio emocional, idade aparente da pele e índices de composição corporal. O processamento é realizado de forma protegida, e os resultados são apresentados de maneira confidencial na tela do celular do usuário. Espelho do Bem-Estar Nas farmácias, estudantes de nutrição acompanham a experiência, explicam os resultados aos consumidores e, com o apoio de profissionais de saúde, identificam necessidades individuais e indicam produtos da Nestlé. O atendimento pode ter continuidade no ambiente digital, por meio da Nina, assistente virtual de Inteligência Artificial desenvolvida pela equipe da Nestlé e treinada por médicos, nutricionistas e outros especialistas, conforme a legislação local. A ferramenta oferece informações sobre hábitos, alimentação e bem-estar, além de orientações sobre soluções nutricionais. O lançamento ocorre em meio à busca dos consumidores por orientação confiável sobre esses produtos. Segundo pesquisa da consultoria McKinsey, 71% esperam experiências personalizadas durante a jornada de compra. A experiência é gratuita e tem finalidade informativa e educativa. Os indicadores são estimativas e não substituem diagnósticos, exames, avaliações clínicas ou acompanhamento médico. Em 2027, a iniciativa deve chegar a todas as regiões do Brasil, primeiro País da América Latina a receber a solução. O projeto incorpora aprendizados da aplicação da tecnologia em outros mercados onde a Nestlé atua, como Europa, Ásia, Estados Unidos e Canadá. Pizza Guys, the Sacramento-based pizza franchise known for its handcrafted specialty pizzas, fresh made dough, and premium ingredients, will celebrate the grand opening of its Newport Beach location on Thursday, Nov. 12, at 3601 Jamboree Rd., Suite 3. The restaurant will be owned and operated by Nader Iskander, who is expanding his business after opening his first Pizza Guys location in Brea in May 2024. Before becoming a Pizza Guys franchisee, Iskander spent years working in a very different industry. Born in Egypt, he moved to Burbank at age 25 and spent years running his own general contracting company. With a longtime passion for cooking, Iskander became interested in Pizza Guys after working with the brand on several construction projects. Impressed by its food quality and innovative restaurant designs, he eventually decided to open his own Pizza Guys restaurant in Brea. “Newport Beach is a community that knows good food, and I’m excited to give them a pizza place they can count on,” said Iskander. “Brea taught me that the real work happens in the details, from making dough fresh every morning to remembering a regular’s usual order. That’s the standard my team and I are bringing to Jamboree Road, and we can’t wait to start serving our new neighbors.” A husband and father of three, Iskander places a high value on family and community. When he opened his Brea restaurant, he chose a location close to home and near a school to better serve local families and students. He hopes to bring that same community-focused approach to Newport Beach. “Nader has shown in Brea exactly what it looks like to run a Pizza Guys the right way, with care for the food, the team and the community,” said Shahpour Nejad, CEO and Founder of Pizza Guys. “We’re excited to see him build on that success with a second location and proud to support him as he brings Pizza Guys to Newport Beach.” To learn more about Pizza Guys Newport Beach and to view their full menu, please visit: pizzaguys.com/location/newport-beach/. The updated concept made its U.S. debut at Captain D’s newest restaurant in San Antonio, Texas. Captain D’s, the nation’s leading fast-casual seafood restaurant, is entering its next phase of growth with the unveiling of a new restaurant design that will begin rolling out in new stores across the country. The updated concept made its U.S. debut at Captain D’s newest restaurant in San Antonio, Texas, giving franchisees and guests a first look at the next generation of the iconic seafood brand. The San Antonio restaurant represents more than the brand’s first location in the market. It showcases a new, more contemporary Captain D’s restaurant, designed to support the company’s continued growth and flexibility across a range of real estate opportunities. With development underway and opportunities emerging in markets including Florida, Ohio, Oklahoma, and Maryland, Captain D’s is looking ahead to where the new design can go next. A New Look Built for Growth The design is a fresh evolution of the Captain D’s experience, combining updated materials and modern design elements while preserving the personality and recognizable identity of the 57-year-old brand. The restaurant features new colors and textures, LED accent lighting, stained concrete floors, and updated backlit exterior signage. The result is a more contemporary and polished environment that gives Captain D’s a refreshed look while maintaining the familiar experience guests know. “We wanted to create a fresh, modern look that reflects where Captain D’s is headed while staying true to who we are,” said Brad Reed, Chief Development Officer for Captain D’s. “It’s more polished and contemporary, but when you walk through the doors, you’ll still recognize Captain D’s. This is an evolution of the brand, not a departure from it.” The San Antonio location also demonstrates the flexibility of the new design in a development setting. Built as an end-cap location with a drive-thru, the restaurant showcases how the updated concept can adapt to different site configurations while delivering a consistent brand experience. The restaurant seats 42 guests and is expected to create approximately 30 to 35 local jobs. San Antonio Marks the Beginning Owned and operated by local franchise partners Ruben Cardenas, Brian Clemens and Dave Peters, the San Antonio restaurant marks the beginning of what the ownership group expects to be a larger presence for Captain D’s in the market. They initially plan to develop three Captain D’s restaurants in the San Antonio area, with plans to eventually grow to as many as 10 locations. “San Antonio is growing tremendously, and we see a real opportunity here,” Cardenas said. “There aren’t a lot of fast seafood options, and we think Captain D’s will be a great addition to the community.” Clemens, who grew up in Florida and has been a longtime Captain D’s fan, was surprised to discover San Antonio did not have a location. That personal connection and knowing the popularity of the brand back home helped inspire the ownership group to bring the brand to his adopted hometown. “I grew up in Florida loving Captain D’s, so when I realized there was an opportunity to bring it to San Antonio, it was an easy decision,” said Clemens. “I’ve missed it and I know people in San Antonio will love the high-quality, generous portions of our hand-battered wild-caught fish from Alaska. Where else can you get a fork and knife meal for $5.99?” A Look at What’s Next While San Antonio provides a first look at how Captain D’s plans to evolve its restaurant footprint, the brand is pursuing rapid domestic and international growth. The new design is already serving as a foundation for future restaurants, giving franchisees a modernized concept that can work across a variety of sites and markets. articles.title: Serasa: demanda das empresas por crédito segue em alta, mas dá sinais de desaceleração
articles.titleKo: Serasa: demanda das empresas por crédito segue em alta, mas dá sinais de desaceleração
articles.originalSummary: A demanda das empresas por crédito começa a dar sinais de arrefecimento, após ter exibido resiliência às restrições provocadas pelo alto nível dos juros. A busca das companhias brasileiras por recursos financeiros cresceu 9,9% no acumulado de 12 meses até setembro, mostra levantamento da Serasa Experian. O movimento foi liderado pelos micro e pequenos negócios (MPEs), com alta de 10%, seguidos de grandes empresas (+8,3%) e médias (+5%). No recorte apenas de setembro, o indicador avançou 0,6% ante igual mês do ano passado. O resultado representa uma forte desaceleração após o avanço de 5,3% em agosto e de 17,6% em julho. “O crescimento também ficou menos disseminado, concentrado em serviços e agropecuária, enquanto comércio e indústria recuaram”, afirma a economista-chefe da Serasa Experian, Camila Abdelmalack. “No entanto, como o indicador apresenta volatilidade e ainda acumula alta de 9,9% em 12 meses, é necessário acompanhar os próximos resultados antes de afirmar uma tendência de desaceleração”, pondera. Entre setores, Serviços liderou a expansão nos 12 meses até setembro, com alta de 15,5%, enquanto Agronegócio subiu 15,1%, Indústria aumentou 6,9% e Comércio teve incremento de 5,6%. No confronto mensal, por outro lado, comércio (-1,4%) e indústria (-3,4%) registraram contração. “A procura por crédito reflete as necessidades de gestão financeira das empresas, mas encontra um mercado mais restritivo, no qual os credores reduzem a exposição ao risco e reforçam os critérios de concessão diante da inadimplência elevada”, ressalta Abdelmalack. Com informação do Estadão de Conteúdo (André Marinho). articles.title: IA muda o ritmo do varejo e exige revisão de processos e controles
articles.titleKo: IA muda o ritmo do varejo e exige revisão de processos e controles
articles.originalSummary: A adoção da Inteligência Artificial no varejo não precisa esperar que as empresas concluam grandes projetos de organização de dados. O caminho passa por começar com aplicações de impacto mensurável, não necessariamente em todas as áreas de uma só vez, testar soluções em ambientes controlados e estabelecer mecanismos de segurança proporcionais aos riscos de cada operação. Essas foram algumas das conclusões após mais uma edição do Quando os Líderes se Encontram, realizada na terça-feira, 10, pela Gouvêa Consulting e Gouvêa Experience, com oferecimento da Kyndryl em parceria com a Google Cloud e a SAP. O evento reuniu executivos do varejo, da indústria e de empresas de tecnologia em dois painéis que discutiram como transformar a experimentação com IA em resultados para o negócio e, ao mesmo tempo, evitar que a expansão das aplicações comprometa a segurança, os custos e a confiabilidade das decisões. Como sair da experimentação e gerar resultado No painel “Da experimentação ao impacto: IA, aplicações e a modernização do varejo”, os participantes defenderam que a escolha dos projetos deve partir das necessidades da operação. O debate envolveu aplicações para aumentar vendas, melhorar margens, reduzir rupturas de estoque e acelerar processos, mas também a dificuldade de transformar ganhos individuais de produtividade em resultados para toda a empresa. Para Ricardo Nastri, vice-presidente de Consultoria da Kyndryl Brasil, a adoção da IA pode combinar iniciativas de resultado mais imediato com projetos de transformação de maior alcance. “O projeto de eficiência ajuda, às vezes, a financiar o projeto de transformação”, afirmou. Essa dinâmica também aparece no Estudo de Modernização 2026 da Kyndryl : entre as empresas de varejo, 50% afirmam reinvestir economias obtidas com a otimização dos custos de nuvem em novas iniciativas de inovação, como IA e novas aplicações, e 47% direcionam esses recursos para outros projetos de modernização. Segundo o executivo, as aplicações menores também contribuem para o aprendizado das equipes e para a criação das condições necessárias à expansão da tecnologia. Ellen Bremm, vice-presidente de Varejo da SAP Brasil, destacou a importância de estabelecer critérios para os investimentos. “Os projetos deveriam ser escolhidos ou priorizados de acordo com o KPI que é relevante para o varejo”, afirmou. A revisão dos processos também apareceu como condição para ampliar os resultados. Rafael Sbampato, diretor de Digital e TI da Riachuelo, chamou a atenção para o fato de que acelerar uma tarefa não significa necessariamente acelerar toda a operação. “Se eu fizesse a peça em 30 segundos e esperasse três meses, eu teria esperado três meses”, exemplificou, ao abordar os desafios do desenvolvimento de produtos. Na MBRF, Marcelo Suárez, diretor de Trade Marketing, Vendas Digitais e Experiência do Cliente, defendeu que o potencial da tecnologia deve ser avaliado também pela capacidade de gerar receita. “Eu prefiro que os 3.500 vendedores que a gente tem vendam mais”, disse, ao comentar a utilização de dados para aprimorar as decisões comerciais. O debate contou ainda com Gutemberg Almeida, industry advisor do Google Cloud, que abordou a importância de estruturar os dados, integrar sistemas e estabelecer controles para que as ferramentas possam atuar nos processos corporativos. Como ampliar a IA sem aumentar os riscos O segundo eixo do encontro tratou de um desafio que ganha relevância à medida que as ferramentas deixam de apenas fornecer informações e passam a executar ações dentro das empresas. No painel “Inovar com confiança: como escalar a IA sem ampliar os riscos?”, os participantes discutiram como conciliar a velocidade exigida pelas áreas de negócios com a proteção dos dados, a gestão dos custos e o monitoramento das decisões automatizadas. Roberto Wajnsztok, sócio-diretor da Gouvêa Consulting, destacou a urgência que caracteriza o setor. “O varejista quer aplicar amanhã, porque precisa bater a meta amanhã”, afirmou

articles.title: KFC and Taco Bell Franchisee Tasty Chick’n Files for Bankruptcy
articles.titleKo: KFC and Taco Bell Franchisee Tasty Chick’n Files for Bankruptcy
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Tasty Chick’n was formed in 2021. Tasty Chick’n, which operates 84 KFC and KFC/Taco Bell restaurants across 10 states, filed for bankruptcy in Houston on Monday. CEO Thomas M. Scott said the company filed to protect the value of its restaurants and to run a court-supervised sale of its assets. It will also look at other ways to restructure on its own, he said. The company runs 75 KFC restaurants and nine KFC/Taco Bell co-branded locations. Florida has the most, with 23, followed by Tennessee with 22. The others are in Virginia, Arkansas, Kentucky, Illinois, Missouri, Alabama, Mississippi and Indiana. Tasty Chick’n was formed in 2021 and built its business through two large purchases. It bought 90 restaurants from Fowler Foods that year and 64 more from JRN, Inc. in 2024. Scott said sales have fallen each year since then. They dropped 11.4 percent in 2024 and 1.4 percent in 2025, and are down another 2.8 percent so far this year, a decline of about 15.6 percent over three years. Meanwhile, food, labor, operating and rent costs rose. The company said its restaurant profit margin shrank from 11.8 percent in 2023 to 4 percent this year, and store-level earnings over the past 12 months fell to about $7.1 million from $12.4 million the year before. As money got tight, Tasty Chick’n began putting off royalty payments to Yum! Brands in mid-2025. It mostly stopped paying them altogether in November 2025. Yum! sent a default notice that December. On September 15, it sent a notice of intent to terminate the franchise agreements, saying Tasty Chick’n owes $15.68 million. Most of that is $7.9 million in advertising contributions and $5.6 million in royalties. Yum! also said the company broke the franchise agreement’s financial reporting rules. Losing the franchise agreements would end the company’s right to use the KFC and Taco Bell names. Scott said that would wipe out the value of the business. It would also put the company in default on its bank loan. That loan is another weight. Tasty Chick’n owes its lenders, led by MidCap Financial Trust, about $67.2 million. It also owes $5 million on a note to JRN. Scott said the company has been talking with both MidCap and Yum! for more than a year but could not get a deal with either, leaving it “caught between” the two. He said the company still hopes for an agreement with both sides. Landlords are also suing. The company faces about 14 real estate lawsuits in Illinois, Florida, Kentucky, Tennessee and Virginia, mostly over unpaid rent, including at stores it has closed or is closing. The suits seek more than $2 million in total. The largest, over a restaurant in Robinson, Illinois, seeks about $1.8 million. Filing for bankruptcy automatically pauses those cases. Nine franchise agreements, tied to closed or closing stores, are being rejected as part of the case, and the company is asking to walk away from the related leases. Another 37 restaurants face remodel or upgrade requirements through 2029, which Scott said add to the company’s costs. The company has hired Guideboat Advisors and Peak Franchise Capital to find buyers. Outreach began in July, and a formal sale process started in October. Tasty Chick’n is marketing the restaurants as one package, market by market, or in combinations, and plans to ask the court to approve bidding rules. Any sale would need court approval and KFC’s consent. Tasty Chick’n employs about 1,646 people. It had about $3.1 million in cash when it filed, and its annual revenue for the year through September was about $194 million. Separate filings show it is asking for a $20 million loan from MidCap to keep operating during the case. articles.title: Durigan defende alíquota da reforma e estima média efetiva de 8,5%
articles.titleKo: Durigan defende alíquota da reforma e estima média efetiva de 8,5%
articles.originalSummary: O ministro da Fazenda, Dario Durigan , afirmou que a reforma tributária trará ganhos permanentes de responsabilidade fiscal, justiça social e transparência ao sistema tributário brasileiro. Ao defender o modelo aprovado, o ministro reiterou que a alíquota máxima estimada para o novo sistema é de 11,3%, mas que a carga efetiva média deverá ficar em 8,5%, enquanto setores beneficiados por regimes diferenciados e parte da população terão tributação menor ou zerada. As declarações foram feitas nesta terça-feira, 17, durante audiência na Comissão de Assuntos Econômicos (CAE) do Senado destinada a discutir a reforma tributária e a metodologia de cálculo da alíquota dos novos tributos sobre o consumo. Segundo Durigan, um dos principais avanços do novo sistema será tornar mais transparente o custo das renúncias fiscais. Pela sistemática aprovada, a concessão de novos benefícios tributários terá impacto direto na alíquota dos tributos sobre o consumo, permitindo que a sociedade e os agentes públicos conheçam os efeitos de cada decisão. “Quando for pautada uma renúncia fiscal, a conta vai ser apresentada de plano. A decisão vai ser inteira”, disse o ministro. Ele ressaltou que a medida permitirá avaliar de forma mais clara os custos de incentivos tributários e os impactos dessas decisões sobre os demais contribuintes. Caráter social Durigan destacou ainda o caráter social da reforma. Entre as medidas citadas estão a tributação zero da cesta básica, o cashback para famílias inscritas no Cadastro Único, além da redução ou isenção de tributos sobre medicamentos, vacinas, itens de saúde da mulher e outros produtos considerados essenciais. Na avaliação dele, a reforma amplia a progressividade do sistema tributário ao reduzir a carga sobre bens essenciais e devolver parte dos tributos pagos por famílias de menor renda. Alíquota efetiva de 8,5% Ao tratar das estimativas para o novo sistema, o ministro voltou a defender os percentuais divulgados pelo governo e pelo Tribunal de Contas da União (TCU). Ele reiterou que os 11,3% divulgados correspondem à alíquota máxima de referência, aplicável aos contribuintes que não se enquadram em qualquer regime favorecido. Segundo ele, a alíquota efetiva média deverá ficar em 8,5%, em razão das reduções previstas para diversos setores da economia, dos regimes diferenciados e das devoluções de tributos para famílias de baixa renda. “11,3% é a alíquota máxima. Quem tem qualquer regime diferenciado, qualquer redução, vai pagar menos. As pessoas mais pobres vão pagar zero. A alíquota média, é de 8,5%.” Revisão anual O ministro acrescentou que a alíquota será revisada anualmente. Pela sistemática aprovada, a Receita Federal fornecerá os dados ao TCU, responsável por aplicar a metodologia prevista na legislação e subsidiar a definição dos percentuais para os anos seguintes. “Isso vai ter uma revisão todo ano. A alíquota está alta? Ótimo, vamos revisitar.” Segundo o ministro, o mecanismo permitirá ajustar benefícios, regimes diferenciados e outros parâmetros do sistema sempre que houver necessidade de recalibrar a alíquota. Responsabilidade Durigan também afirmou que a reforma exigirá responsabilidade fiscal dos três Poderes. Segundo ele, novas isenções aprovadas pelo Legislativo ou decisões judiciais que ampliem benefícios tributários poderão elevar a alíquota geral do Imposto sobre Valor Agregado (IVA) para compensar a perda de arrecadação. “Não há mágica na economia. Nós vamos ter que ser responsáveis todos, inclusive o Supremo, inclusive o Judiciário, porque a conta vai vir.” Entenda A Contribuição sobre Bens e Serviços (CBS), tributo federal criado na reforma tributária, substituirá o PIS/Pasep e a Cofins a partir de 2027. Ao lado do Imposto sobre Bens e Serviços (IBS), de competência estadual e municipal, formará o novo modelo de Imposto sobre Valor Agregado (IVA) dual do País. articles.title: The Gyro Project Opening in NYC’s Union Square Neighborhood
articles.titleKo: The Gyro Project Opening in NYC’s Union Square Neighborhood
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . The Gyro Project, a fast-fine Greek restaurant bringing authentic street food flavors to a modern setting, will celebrate the opening of its newest New York City location at 107 East 14th Street in Manhattan’s Union Square neighborhood on Thursday, December 3 at 11am with an official Ribbon Cutting Ceremony. The opening marks another milestone in the brand’s continued expansion throughout New York City, bringing its signature Greek flavors and approachable dining experience to one of Manhattan’s busiest shopping, dining and cultural destinations. Located just steps from Union Square, the approximately 600-square-foot restaurant will feature 16 indoor seats and offer The Gyro Project’s signature menu for dine-in, takeout and delivery. Open daily from 10am to 2am, the new location will bring the brand’s fast-fine Greek offerings to the neighborhood throughout the day and late into the night, serving as a convenient destination for nearby residents, students, professionals and late-night diners. The thoughtfully designed interior will blend warm wood finishes with custom-designed wallpaper, neutral wall tiles and woven chairs, creating a welcoming, contemporary atmosphere that balances natural textures with understated design details. The Union Square location will feature a Build-Your-Own Froyo Bar, serving as The Gyro Project’s third location – including Hell’s Kitchen and Garment District – to provide this offering. Guests can also expect The Gyro Project’s lineup of Greek favorites, including classic gyro pita wraps featuring chicken, pork and lamb & beef; hearty platters served with rice, salad and pita; traditional dips such as tzatziki and hummus, soups including traditional Greek avgolemono; loaded Greek fries; fresh salads; and the brand’s signature Greek frozen yogurt. Founded by childhood friends and restaurateurs George Tenedios and Spiro Kokkosis, The Gyro Project was created to fill a void for high-quality Greek cuisine in New York and New Jersey. Since debuting its first location in Fort Lee, New Jersey, in July 2023, the brand has built a loyal following for its signature pita wraps, mixed grill platters, mezedes, specialty fries, rotisserie chicken and Greek froyo – all rooted in authentic recipes and bold Mediterranean flavors. “We’re excited to bring The Gyro Project to Union Square, a neighborhood that has such an incredible mix of energy, culture and community,” said George Tenedios , co-owner of The Gyro Project and recently appointed Archon of the Ecumenical Patriarchate . “As we continue growing throughout New York City, we’re always looking for ways to make each location feel connected to its surroundings. In this lively neighborhood, our extended hours will allow us to serve guests well beyond the traditional lunch and dinner rush.” The Union Square opening follows the brand’s October 15 debut in Hell’s Kitchen at 600 9th Avenue. The opening also builds on The Gyro Project’s growing Manhattan presence, with restaurants serving neighborhoods including the Upper East Side, Upper West Side, Murray Hill, Midtown East, the Garment District and Hudson Yards. articles.titleKo: Amazon contrata 12 mil temporários para a Black Friday e abre 3.500 vagas permanentes em SP
articles.originalSummary: A Amazon contratou mais de 12 mil trabalhadores temporários no Brasil para atravessar a Black Friday. A varejista chega ao período de maior demanda do ano com 350 centros logísticos, número que inclui mais de 120 unidades abertas desde a edição anterior da data. A média é de duas novas instalações por semana. O objetivo é sustentar a promessa de entrega rápida nos 100% dos municípios do País. “A Black Friday é o momento em que os clientes de todo o Brasil mais contam com a gente, e esses trabalhadores são as pessoas que tornam possível uma entrega rápida e confiável durante o nosso período de maior movimento”, afirma Mireille Schoenardie, líder de Recursos Humanos para Operações da Amazon no Brasil. As vagas temporárias cobrem o salto de pedidos típico da data, mas existe a possibilidade de efetivação. Em 2026, mais de 5 mil pessoas que entraram como temporárias foram efetivadas. Foi o caso de Yorrana Laura, que entrou na Amazon como temporária durante a Black Friday de 2025 e hoje é Assistente de Processos. “Entrei na Amazon como trabalhadora temporária em recebimentos durante a Black Friday. Poucos meses depois, conquistei uma promoção para assistente de processos. O conselho que dou a quem está chegando agora é manter o comprometimento e o foco: crescer aqui é uma possibilidade real para todos”, afirma. Thiago Bittencourt também começou durante uma Black Friday anterior e hoje atua como embaixador, responsável por acolher e treinar novos trabalhadores. “Cheguei muito nervoso e apreensivo no início, mas fui acolhido por toda a equipe. Além de me efetivar e depois me tornar embaixador para treinar os recém-chegados, a experiência transformou o meu lado pessoal “, afirma Thiago. Mais de 3.500 vagas em São Paulo Fora da leva sazonal, a Amazon abre mais de 3.500 vagas efetivas na Grande São Paulo. O pacote inclui convênio médico e odontológico desde o primeiro dia, plano de progressão salarial, bônus, desconto para funcionários e o Programa de Apoio ao Empregado (PAE). Os candidatos devem ter 18 anos ou mais e podem se inscrever no site . articles.title: Outback Cofounder Tim Gannon on Partnerships, and Lessons Learned Along the Way
articles.titleKo: Outback Cofounder Tim Gannon on Partnerships, and Lessons Learned Along the Way
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . Food was always central to Outback's early premise. When Tim Gannon moved to Tampa to join his future Outback Steakhouse partners, he arrived with $37 in his pocket. He had sold his polo saddle for gas money and left a job in New Orleans to pursue an opportunity based around who he’d work with , not for . The original plan was relatively modest: open four restaurants. But in the end, Outback grew to 1,300 units and one of the industry’s true icons was born. In a conversation on QSR Uncut (see full episode below), he reflected on the decisions behind the brand’s growth, from the creation of the most-famous appetizer there is in the Bloomin’ Onion to the importance of ownership, hospitality, and getting the word out when you’re just starting. Here are five leadership lessons from the conversation. 1. Choose partners who bring different strengths Before joining Outback, Gannon says his boss offered to pay off his debts, buy him a home, and give him a financial cushion. The offer was worth about $1 million, but it didn’t include equity. Gannon turned it down. He wanted to build something with partners rather than continue working for someone else. “The key was to make money with someone, not for someone,” he said. In Tampa, he found partners who brought different skills to the venture. Gannon focused on food, while Chris Sullivan and Bob Basham developed approaches to incentives, compensation, and operations. He recalls staying with Basham while getting settled in Tampa. Looking back, Gannon considers those relationships central to Outback’s success. “I can’t tell you how important having the right partners is,” he said. The lesson: Look for partners who share your ambition, complement your skills, and are willing to build something together. 2. Create something distinctive by connecting ideas The Bloomin’ Onion began with curiosity about flavor and presentation. While working in New Orleans, Gannon studied how flavors were combined and watched the city’s chefs at work. Along with colleagues, he explored cookbooks for fresh ideas. One Japanese version showed how onions and other vegetables could be cut into flowers. Gannon took inspiration from the presentation, made it edible, and combined it with New Orleans spices. The result became Outback’s signature appetizer. Gannon says the product’s complexity helped make it difficult to duplicate. The seasoning requires a particular blend, and the size of the onion creates operational challenges: Outback built its kitchens with the equipment needed to prepare it at volume. But the idea itself was also memorable. As Gannon phrased it, an item can become attached to a brand in a way that is difficult to transfer elsewhere. The lesson: Originality doesn’t always mean inventing from nothing. It can come from combining influences in a way customers recognize as your own, and building the operation to deliver it consistently. 3. A good product still needs people to discover it When the first Outback opened, business was slow. Gannon recalls a difficult location, little marketing, and customers who didn’t know what to expect from an Australian-themed steakhouse. When Sullivan asked whether he had gotten the food right, Gannon disagreed. The food wasn’t the setback, he believed. People simply didn’t know the restaurant existed. The team began looking for ways to get the product in front of the community. One early effort involved cooking Bloomin’ Onions outside a local radio DJ’s office and bringing them in fresh for him to try on air. Gannon remembers cooking by flashlight early in the morning. The exposure introduced the restaurant to customers. Gannon also recalls overhearing diners at a nearby pizzeria discussing the appetizer and saying they couldn’t wait to tell their neighbors. That conversation gave him hope Outback could make it. The lesson: Don’t assume a strong prod

articles.title: Your Guests Still Love You. So Why Aren’t They Spending?
articles.titleKo: Your Guests Still Love You. So Why Aren’t They Spending?
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Consumers today are affected by the largest credit card debt per household ever experienced. Guests might love your restaurant brand more than ever. They might recommend you to their friends, give you glowing reviews, and rank you above every competitor in your category. And yet, they may be visiting half as often. Restaurant leaders know consumers are feeling the financial squeeze. They’re watching transaction counts, average checks, and visit frequency while trying to determine how much of the decline is economic and how much reflects changing brand preference. Yet the loyalty metrics they rely on don’t always make that distinction clear. It creates a serious challenge for operators trying to understand the performance of their brands. It also deserves consideration when evaluating one of the most influential theories in loyalty research. Loyalty Metrics Aren’t Perfect In a 2011 Harvard Business Review article, Timothy Keiningham and his fellow researchers challenged conventional wisdom in how loyalty is measured and evaluated. The research found that popular loyalty measures, including guest satisfaction and Net Promoter Score (NPS), had surprisingly weak relationships with how consumers allocated their spending in reality. Their alternative, named the Wallet Allocation Rule, demonstrated that a brand’s relative ranking among competitors was substantially more predictive of its share of guest spending. The principle is compelling. Here’s how it plays out: A guest might be perfectly satisfied with your restaurant while preferring three competitors. Their satisfaction tells you relatively little about how much of their business you’ll actually capture. Keiningham’s research helped expose the dangerous assumption that satisfied guests are simultaneously commercially loyal guests. However, restaurant leaders should be equally skeptical of treating share of wallet as the definitive measure of loyalty. The research was conducted before a global pandemic dismantled established dining routines. It was conducted before digital ordering became such a dominant force in restaurant transactions, and before years of inflation fundamentally changed how consumers evaluate everyday purchases. The original principle remains valuable, but the conditions under which guests act on their preferences have changed considerably. And it’s complicated efforts to explain declining restaurant spending through competitive preference alone. Guests Aren’t Necessarily Leaving. They’re Spending Less. According to the National Restaurant Association’s third-quarter 2026 consumer research, 50 percent of consumers reported greater difficulty covering their expenses than a year earlier. Forty percent said they were using more discounts and value promotions than usual. And it’s absolutely showing up in purchasing behavior. To compound the issue, McKinsey’s January 2026 restaurant research found that consumers planning to reduce restaurant spending generally preferred cutting back at their favorite restaurants through smaller orders, cheaper items, or promotions rather than abandoning those restaurants for lower-priced competitors. Suffice to say, the game has changed notably. Here’s how that plays out: A guest who previously visited your restaurant weekly may now visit twice a month. They might skip the appetizer or share an entrée with someone else. Their average check declines, their annual spending falls, and their transaction frequency deteriorates. By all conventional commercial measures, that guest looks less loyal. Yet their preference for your brand may be entirely intact. This is where the distinction between brand preference and economic capacity becomes a noticeable and critical factor. articles.title: Franchise Executive Kendall Ware Releases New Book
articles.titleKo: Franchise Executive Kendall Ware Releases New Book
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . At the center of the book is FranShip, Ware's philosophy that blends strong franchise relationships, genuine partnership and authentic friendship. Franchise brands chase unit growth, while the relationships that make that growth sustainable quietly erode. In his new book, “ Built for Franchising: The Advantage Is FranShip ,” franchise executive Kendall Ware, founder and CEO of FranShip Brands, lays out a blueprint for building franchise systems on partnership instead of transaction, with a foreword by 13-time New York Times bestselling author Don Yaeger. Published by Entrepreneur Books and distributed by Simon & Schuster, the book is now available through national and independent book retailers. Ware argues that the strength of the relationship between franchisor and franchisee is the single biggest variable in whether a brand lasts. Strong products, airtight agreements and large ad budgets cannot make up for a network where trust has broken down. When franchisors serve franchisees so franchisees can better serve guests, and both sides commit to the same goal, the payoff shows up in unit profitability, guest loyalty and long-term brand value. “Most franchise problems look like operations problems, but look closer and you’ll find a relationship that stopped working,” Ware said. “When franchisors and franchisees agree on the destination, which is earning the guest’s next visit, a disagreement becomes a conversation instead of a power struggle.” At the center of the book is FranShip ® , Ware’s philosophy that blends strong franchise relationships, genuine partnership and authentic friendship. The FranShip Framework ® brings it to life through a five-level blueprint modeled on building a house: culturally aligned people as the foundation, operational excellence as the four walls, financial optimization as the ceiling, community marketing as the second story and brand amplification as the roof. Each level spells out what franchisors and franchisees each owe the system, and the first five chapters close with fireside conversations with leading operators, including Greg Flynn of Flynn Group and Cinnabon co-founder Greg Komen. Ware pairs the framework with practical tools. The RETAIN Model™ (recruit, engage, train, assimilate, involve and nurture) gives operators a structure for keeping frontline teams in high-turnover businesses. FEES: Franchisees Expect Exceptional Support ® reframes the most common source of franchise friction, and the 777 Rule shows leaders how to communicate important changes seven times, through seven methods, for seven learning styles. He also makes the case for awarding franchises to aligned operators rather than selling them to anyone with a check. Drawing on more than two decades in franchising, Ware writes from both sides of the table. He started busing tables at 16 and, before turning 35, served as CEO, president or COO of seven brands, including Cinnabon, Carvel, Orange Leaf Frozen Yogurt and Walk-On’s Sports Bistreaux. He has also been a franchisee twice. The book draws on that record, from a Walk-On’s training redesign that saved the average franchisee more than $100,000 in pre-opening payroll to an Orange Leaf turnaround in which initiative adoption rose from 40% to 95% after the team invested in its franchisee relationships. Throughout the book, Ware challenges the assumption that signed agreements and unit counts are the measure of a healthy franchise system. He shows how growth that outruns support leads to closures, how cutting labor to protect margins can shrink revenue and how transparency about failed initiatives builds the credibility that makes the next one succeed. articles.originalSummary: Hospitality insolvencies fell by 24% in October, with industry figures suggesting operators are holding on through the final months of the year ahead of the Christmas trading period. The latest company insolvency statistics, published today, show that 210 accommodation and food service businesses entered insolvency in October 2026, down from 275 in September and 32% lower than the 307 recorded in October 2025.
