articles.title: Burger King is Rebuilding its Restaurants. It Wants Customers to Help Decide Where
articles.titleKo: Burger King is Rebuilding its Restaurants. It Wants Customers to Help Decide Where
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Burger King president Tom Curtis received 120,000 calls and voicemails after posting his phone number in mid-February . Feedback typically unfolded a couple of ways (in addition to a few marriage proposals): Somebody suggested what the chain needed to do. Or, they mentioned the location itself. Curtis found that latter loop difficult to visualize. So, starting in June, he hit the road and asked customers, once again, to be honest about Burger King. Curtis didn’t pick rundown or tired locations off a predetermined map; he randomly walked in and got customers to open up. By now, he had a lot of experience, to put it lightly, in doing so. “A lot of times they would tell you, ‘It doesn’t make me feel good about my community to come here,’” Curtis says in an interview with QSR magazine . “It doesn’t make me feel good about my community to even drive by here. And I just wish that the commitment that you guys had to your menu and your food and your Whopper was matched by your commitment to my community’s sentiment.” “That,” Curtis heard, “would move me the most.” Burger King rolled the tape on Curtis’ road trip and captured experiences for a new campaign launched Tuesday that will place customer responses at the center. In addition to Curtis fielding replies on-site, the brand debuted a “ ReBuildMyBK.com ” website where guests can offer thoughts on their local restaurant and help Burger King pinpoint stores in need of TLC. Burger King president Tom Curtis is taking feedback once again. This time, it’s around the brand’s store assets. And as far as Burger King has come since launching “Reclaim the Flame” in September 2021, this is one corner of its turnaround with whitespace. The brand is about 60 percent into a modern re-image. As of September 30, parent company Restaurant Brands International funded $198 million out of up to $550 million set aside for “Royal Reset” improvements, which include remodels, relocations, restaurant technology kitchen equipment, and building enhancements. Burger King in 2023 unveiled a “Sizzle” design and later developed a catalogue for operators to expand the implementation of the unit’s elements. It’s no grand mystery why Burger King wants to accelerate. Of updated restaurants disclosed via its 2026 FDD, 964 underwent a full remodel and 67 scrape and rebuilds. The average sales uplift was double-digits for each, but north of 25 percent for demolished restaurants. Full remodels appreciated an 11.9 percent average sales uplift, while scrape and rebuilds were at 26 percent. Stores that underwent a conversion to a double drive-thru observed average sales hikes of 16.8 percent (10.6 percent without). And restaurants that fixed from legacy to “modern image” posted average sales growth of 13.8 percent. Units from Burger King’s “20/20 Light” to a new look achieved 10.2 percent. With Sizzle, those garnered upticks of 14.9 percent. Here’s a deeper breakdown . But to Curtis’ point, sentiment can’t always be number crunched. You have to ask people how they feel. Curtis says he heard “good, bad, and otherwise” as he traveled. He witnessed old units. New ones. Sizzles. Upgraded, but not Sizzles. And, naturally, some “really rough” Burger Kings. The campaign chronicled Curtis’ trips to five markets—Columbus, Georgia; Cleveland; Chicago; Phoenix; and Las Vegas. He observed everything, and Curtis was a seasoned listening pro at this point. When Burger King opened Curtis’ hotline last winter, he sat with director of communications Kristen Viersen on the porch of his house and prepared. It was key, he says, to ensure he wouldn’t overpromise and underdeliver. It can be easier to agree with critics than host an open dialogue on what to improve. articles.title: GEN Korean BBQ Prepares for Layoffs as it Transitions to CPG Business
articles.titleKo: GEN Korean BBQ Prepares for Layoffs as it Transitions to CPG Business
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . A definitive asset purchase agreement has not been signed, and the final terms are still being negotiated. GEN Korean BBQ plans to dismantle much of the infrastructure it built to support years of restaurant expansion, targeting a 75 percent reduction in corporate overhead. Layoffs are set to begin in the fourth quarter. The sweeping restructuring comes as the company works to sell most of its restaurants and transform itself into a CPG business. The brand eyes a much smaller organization focused on getting Korean barbecue products into grocery stores and American homes. “GEN today carries the corporate structure of a company that was opening 10 restaurants a year. The company we are becoming needs a fraction of that,” chairman and CEO David Kim said during the company’s Q3 earnings call earlier this month. Kim did not specify how many corporate employees would lose their jobs. Some restaurant-support functions are expected to transfer with the locations being sold, and GEN is renegotiating or terminating office leases, systems, and other contracts that will no longer be necessary. “Every role in the new GEN must earn its place by growing CPG or keeping us compliant,” Kim said. The cost-cutting initiative is tied to GEN’s previously announced agreement to sell 47 U.S. restaurants to Chubby Cattle Group for up to $100 million. The companies signed a binding letter of intent in October, outlining a transaction that would transfer restaurant operations and lease obligations to Chubby Cattle over time. A definitive asset purchase agreement has not been signed, and the final terms are still being negotiated. GEN would continue operating each restaurant until its transfer is completed. Under the proposed deal, GEN would retain ownership of its brand, its CPG business, and its restaurant in Cerritos, California, which would support training and product development. The company would also keep its existing 49 percent ownership interest in five Chubby Group restaurants through a separate joint venture. The potential sale represents a dramatic reversal for a chain that previously envisioned an aggressive national expansion. In early 2025, GEN was targeting 75 restaurants by the end of 2026. Its priorities have since shifted as restaurant sales weakened, operating losses mounted, and its retail business gained traction. The financial pressure continued in Q3. Revenue declined 3.3 percent to $48.7 million from $50.4 million a year earlier. Operating losses widened to $6 million from $3.7 million, and the company’s net loss increased to $5.5 million from $3.6 million. Adjusted EBITDA was a loss of approximately $600,000, compared with a loss of $200,000 in the prior-year period. GEN also faces a growing debt burden. Total outstanding debt reached $26.8 million at the end of September, up from $14.6 million at the end of 2025. Cash and cash equivalents stood at $2.9 million. The company expects proceeds from the proposed restaurant transaction to help reduce debt. The restructuring would leave GEN with a business that requires significantly less investment in real estate, construction, and restaurant staffing. Its retail products are manufactured through partners in several U.S. states and South Korea, allowing the company to expand production without building its own facilities. GEN is targeting a $40 million annualized CPG revenue run rate by the end of 2027, with Kim suggesting that figure could rise as the company secures additional retail partnerships. The brand’s frozen Korean barbecue meats are already available through retailers including Albertsons, Safeway, Vons, Stater Bros., Smart & Final, Save Mart, Bristol Farms, and select Costco regions. articles.title: Galpão Gaucho Brazilian Steakhouse Unveils Major Expansion
articles.titleKo: Galpão Gaucho Brazilian Steakhouse Unveils Major Expansion
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . Family-owned and operated Galpão Gaucho Brazilian Steakhouse has completed a 5,394-square-foot expansion, bringing its restaurant to nearly 12,000 square feet with redesigned dining areas and event spaces for celebrations, corporate entertaining and social gatherings. Designed to enhance both everyday dining and private events, the expansion allows Galpão Gaucho to welcome more guests, accommodate larger parties and host multiple gatherings simultaneously while preserving the attentive service and warm Southern Brazilian hospitality guests have come to appreciate. The transformation reflects Galpão Gaucho’s continued commitment to the Bay Area and coincides with the brand’s 10th anniversary Year of Celebration, honoring a decade of authentic Southern Brazilian churrasco traditions and memorable experiences shared around the table. “Churrasco has always been about bringing people together,” said Jovani Gava, founder and director of operations at Galpão Gaucho Brazilian Steakhouse. “In Southern Brazil, meals are social occasions where family and friends gather, conversations flow and hospitality takes center stage. As we celebrate 10 years of Galpão Gaucho, these enhancements allow us to bring even more people together, with spaces that feel just as personal for an intimate dinner as they do for a gathering of a hundred.” Throughout the restaurant, rich wood-paneled walls, statement chandeliers and warm finishes create an inviting atmosphere. Near the piano, signature white leather seating provides a comfortable setting to enjoy dinner, cocktails and live music. The new private and semi-private dining areas feature sleek upholstered chairs in contrasting shades of brown and black, offering added comfort for business meetings, corporate events and celebrations. The restaurant now offers five private dining and event spaces accommodating groups of 10 to 100 guests. Glass partitions, floor-to-ceiling curtains and flexible room configurations allow for gatherings of varying sizes, including one space that converts from two private rooms into a single venue. Long banquet-style tables, complimentary audiovisual capabilities and large-screen TVs support everything from executive meetings and presentations to rehearsal dinners and holiday parties. At the heart of the expansion remains Galpão Gaucho’s signature rodizio experience, where gaucho chefs continuously carve 17 selections from the grill tableside. Guests also enjoy a gourmet salad bar featuring more than 45 offerings, Brazilian-inspired specialties, signature side dishes, handcrafted desserts and a curated wine program. For private events, hosts can tailor beverage service to their gathering by preselecting wine bottles or wines by the glass, limiting selections to signature cocktails or standard-tier drinks – or setting a designated number of drinks per guest. Through December 31, 2026, qualifying private dining and event reservations are eligible for exclusive Year of Celebration rewards for both organizers and attendees. Details and eligibility requirements are available on the Year of Celebration page. For more information or to reserve a private dining experience, corporate event or celebration, visit GalpaoGauchoUSA.com. articles.title: Three thinking: Max Venning on his new oyster and martini bar
articles.titleKo: Three thinking: Max Venning on his new oyster and martini bar
articles.originalSummary: As Three Sheets turns 10, Max Venning is gearing up to launch Berryman’s in Dalston. And it’s standing room only. Max Venning is marking a decade of Three Sheets with the launch of Berryman’s, a new martini and oyster bar in Dalston. Having built an internationally recognised cocktail bar brand along with his brother Noel from an 18-seat venue in East London, the pair are looking to the next chapter while remaining focused on what they do best: making great drinks. Since opening Three Sheets in 2016, the brothers have expanded into Soho, developed a broader food and drink offering and navigated the increasingly challenging economics of running independent bars. Yet, despite their growing portfolio and ambitions for further expansion, their philosophy remains rooted in the same principles that underpinned the original venue.

articles.title: Birley Bakery’s Francesco Coratella Represents The United Kingdom In The Panettone World Cup 2026
articles.titleKo: Birley Bakery’s Francesco Coratella Represents The United Kingdom In The Panettone World Cup 2026
articles.originalSummary: Birley Bakery’s Francesco Coratella Represents the UK at the Panettone World Cup 2026 Francesco Coratella, Executive Pastry Chef at London-based Birley Bakery, 5 Hertford Street and Oswald’s, represented the United Kingdom at the Panettone World Cup 2026, which took place on 7–8 November at the Melià Milan. Birley Bakery’s Francesco Coratella Represents the UK at the Panettone World Cup 2026 Francesco Coratella, Executive Pastry Chef at London-based Birley Bakery, 5 Hertford Street and Oswald’s, represented the United Kingdom at the Panettone World Cup 2026, which took place on 7–8 November at the Melià Milan. The competition celebrates the history and craft of panettone, with 19 countries represented in the world final, highlighting the growing popularity of the traditional Italian bake beyond national borders. Francesco competed in the Best Traditional Panettone category, marking the second edition of the competition in which he has represented the UK. Following two years of selections and shortlisting, the fifth edition of the Panettone World Cup brought together international pastry talent. The selections have developed into events dedicated to panettone culture, organised in collaboration with Italian Embassies in participating countries and under the patronage of the Italian Trade Agency (ITA). Products are evaluated anonymously by rotating juries comprising renowned pastry chefs. A key ingredient in Birley’s signature panettone is lievito madre , or mother yeast, which is nurtured by Francesco and requires regular feeding with flour and water to maintain its strength and activity. Rather than using commercial yeast, Birley relies solely on this mother yeast, which is more than 60 years old and has been passed down through two generations of Italian pastry chefs. The fermentation process, using a natural culture made from flour and water fermented with wild yeast and lactic acid bacteria from the environment, creates the panettone’s complex flavour and texture while also improving its shelf life. Birley panettones are available to order online and in-store, with click-and-collect and nationwide delivery options. Panettones are available for pre-order online now and in-store, for click-and-collect, and with nationwide delivery.

articles.title: Celebrate Christmas The Humble Way
articles.titleKo: Celebrate Christmas The Humble Way
articles.originalSummary: This Christmas, from the 10th November to 23rd December, the Humble Group is inviting all to celebrate the festive period the best way we know how – with great food, flowing wine, and the people who matter most. Whether planning an office Christmas party, a cosy family gathering, or a festive feast with friends, Humble Grape and Vivat Bacchus are ready with open arms, warm hospitality, and a glass (or three) of wine. EARLY BIRD BONUS To kick off the season in style, the Humble Group is offering an early bird treat for those getting in the festive spirit a little sooner. If you book a Christmas party for eight or more people in November and dine from the festive party menu between the 16th and 30th of November, the Humble Group will throw in a glass of fizz for all. FESTIVE FEASTING AT HUMBLE GRAPE At Humble Grape, the festive menu is all about indulgent seasonal flavours, created especially for larger group celebrations. We’re talking rich duck and chestnut terrine, and the ultimate traditional roast turkey dinner with all the trimmings – Roast potatoes, maple-glazed carrots, braised red cabbage, sprouts & gravy . Not feeling turkey? No problem. A juicy tomahawk steak served with all the festive sides brings a modern twist to the table, perfect for those craving something a little different. Costing £60 per person at our city locations, and £35 per person at our neighborhood sites: Battersea & Islington. MEET UNDER THE MISTLETOE For the wine enthusiasts (or those excited to learn more), Humble Grape is hosting a series of Mistletoe and Wine tasting evenings. These relaxed and sociable events will start with a surprise welcome drink, followed by a guided tasting of six organic winter wines – from full-bodied reds to complex, wintery whites, all led by the in-house wine team. It’s a great way to discover new favourites and welcome in the holiday season. Tastings will run from 6.30 PM to 8.30 PM across three of our venues: Liverpool Street – Monday 7th December Battersea – Tuesday 8th December Bow Lane – Wednesday 9th December A SOUTH-AFRICAN CHRISTMAS AT VIVAT BACCHUS Meanwhile, at Vivat Bacchus , Christmas is getting a South African twist – bringing bold flavours, big energy, and warm hospitality to the table. The menu is served family style, so everyone can get involved and dig in. Expect delicious dishes like beef carpaccio with biltong aioli, turkey & boerewors sosatie, and brannas & Coke gammon all served with festive sides like braised red cabbage , Cape Malay sprouts and rooibos cranberries, cinnamon and honey butternut squash and more.. To finish it off? The much-loved South African peppermint tart – sweet, nostalgic, and totally irresistible. If you’ve never had a South African-style Christmas, now’s your chance to say “lekker” and dive right in, all for £60 per person. GIFTING MADE EASY For those looking for the perfect bottle of something special or a last-minute gift, pop into Humble Grape or Vivat Bacchus and find the perfect Christmas present. Browse an incredible selection of wines from around the world, all ideal for gifting (or keeping for yourself!). It might be a thoughtful bottle for a friend, a gift voucher, or a subscription to The Humble Club for a wine lover in your life. Join the Club and get two glasses of wine per week, 10% off tickets, birthday perks and more – all for £25 per month! Or maybe find something a bit more refined for corporate gifting? The Humble Group offers bulk sales of wines, ideal for events, client gifts, and company celebrations. So, swap the socks for sauvignon – whatever it is, the Humble Group has you covered. Every Humble Group experience is designed to capture the spirit of Christmas – simply book, relax, and leave the rest to the experts. Learn more at humblegrape.co.uk/christmas and www.viv

articles.title: Wendy’s Proposes $52 Million Deal to Acquire 163 Restaurants from Bankrupt Franchisee
articles.titleKo: Wendy’s Proposes $52 Million Deal to Acquire 163 Restaurants from Bankrupt Franchisee
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . The proposed deal represents a major step in Wendy’s effort to resolve Meritage’s bankruptcy and strengthen the performance of restaurants that have struggled financially. Wendy’s is preparing to make one of the largest acquisitions of franchised restaurants in its history, offering approximately $52 million to purchase 163 locations and related real estate from bankrupt operator Meritage Hospitality Group. The proposed transaction would give Wendy’s corporate control of a substantial portfolio as the burger chain works to improve stabilize its franchise system and reverse declining customer traffic. Under the proposed settlement, Wendy’s would serve as the stalking horse bidder for the 163 restaurants, meaning it sets the baseline offer for an potential upcoming auction. READ MORE : Wendy’s is Going Back to Basics to Save its Business Major Wendy’s Franchisee Significantly Cuts Footprint During Bankruptcy What the Meritage Chapter 11 Teaches Restaurant Franchisees Major Wendy’s Franchisee Files for Bankruptcy Wendy’s is offering approximately $45.9 million for the 163 restaurants, after a $7.2 million credit is deducted from the original $53.1 million price. The company would also pay $6 million for four real estate properties, bringing the total proposed purchase price to approximately $51.9 million. The transaction has not been finalized and remains subject to bankruptcy court approval, competing offers, and other closing conditions. The filing calls for the purchase agreement to be executed by November 21 and the transaction to close no later than January 5. The proposed deal represents a major step in Wendy’s effort to resolve Meritage’s bankruptcy and strengthen the performance of restaurants that have struggled financially. During the company’s Q3 earnings call, CEO Bob Wright said the chain had signed a letter of intent to acquire up to 163 Meritage restaurants. He described the situation as unfortunate, given the companies’ longstanding relationship, but said Wendy’s saw an opportunity to improve operations. “We’ve been an asset-light strategy for a long time. This will be, we think, one of the largest, if not the largest acquisition of franchise to company restaurants in the company’s history, certainly in a long, long time,” Wright said. The restaurants Wendy’s intends to acquire are concentrated in markets where the company already operates corporate locations. That geographic overlap would allow the chain to use its existing field organization and operating experience to support the acquired stores without building an entirely new infrastructure. Wright also sees an opportunity for Wendy’s to benefit financially as the restaurants recover. “We get to drive and enjoy the benefit of the turnaround of those markets, leveraging the G&A and the organizational structure that we already have in the field,” he said. “If we do reposition them back into the franchise system at some point in the future, we anticipate there’d be a gain on that sale, which is another point of financial leverage for us.” Although Wendy’s could eventually sell the restaurants to franchisees, Wright declined to commit to that approach or provide a timetable. He stressed that the proposed acquisition is a deliberate investment in restaurant performance, not simply an effort to facilitate a transfer of ownership. The remainder of Meritage’s restaurant portfolio is expected to transition to other franchisees through the bankruptcy process. Wright said those restaurants are concentrated in markets better suited to franchise ownership, and potential buyers could include both existing and new Wendy’s operators. The agreement also allows approved franchisees to submit higher or better offers for the 163 restaurants Wendy’s intends to purchase. articles.title: Contemporary Indian Restaurant Bar O Bar to Open in Cary, North Carolina
articles.titleKo: Contemporary Indian Restaurant Bar O Bar to Open in Cary, North Carolina
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . Bar O Bar, a new contemporary Indian restaurant rooted in the culinary traditions of South India, will open in December in Cary, bringing a refined yet approachable take on Indian dining to the Triangle. Built around the idea of being “Perfectly Indian,” Bar O Bar celebrates the depth and diversity of Indian cuisine, with a particular emphasis on South Indian flavors and traditions. The restaurant’s name draws from “barobar,” meaning “perfect” in several Indian languages, reflecting a philosophy of balance that extends across its food, cocktails, design and hospitality. While Indian cuisine in the U.S. is often associated with a familiar collection of North Indian dishes, Bar O Bar will introduce guests to a broader range of regional flavors. Much of the menu will place a special focus on South Indian culinary traditions, built on ingredients such as fresh coconut, mustard seeds, black pepper and curry leaves, and techniques such as fermentation, alongside familiar favorites from other regions of India. “We created Bar O Bar to showcase the depth, diversity and creativity of Indian cuisine beyond what many guests may have experienced,” said Sai Ancha, co-owner of Bar O Bar. “Cary felt like the perfect home for that vision. It’s a community that values great food and genuine hospitality, and we want every guest to leave having discovered something new, while feeling welcomed like family.” Chef Vikash Vumudi leads the kitchen, with international experience in Michelin-recognized kitchens. Vumudi honed his craft at Sindhu, the acclaimed restaurant from Michelin-starred chef Atul Kochhar in England, before working as a development chef alongside celebrity chef Ajay Chopra, where he helped conceptualize and launch new restaurant ventures. His approach centers on technique, ingredient integrity and authentic flavor, with contemporary presentations that remain rooted in Indian culinary tradition. “South Indian cooking is all about balance: the brightness of tamarind, the warmth of black pepper and the richness of fresh coconut. My approach is to let those flavors shine through precise technique and exceptional ingredients,” Chef Vikash Vumudi said. “I am honored to introduce Cary to dishes that many guests may be experiencing for the first time and to share the depth and vibrancy of South Indian cuisine.” The opening menu will feature Donne biryani and Ghee & Gunpowder, along with Noor and Konkan, two cocktails inspired by Indian desserts. The restaurant’s philosophy extends beyond the plate. Interiors by Anil Cherukuri, principal architect of Anilam Architects, blend contemporary design with timeless Indian craftsmanship. Handcrafted furniture sourced from Rajasthan, natural stone, warm timber, antique brass and rich textiles come together in an intimate, sophisticated space that feels distinctly Indian. Bar O Bar is part of “Sama Hospitality,” also owners of Fusion Nine, the modern Indian restaurant in Morrisville known for its blend of regional Indian and Indo-Chinese dishes, craft cocktails and welcoming, contemporary atmosphere. Bar O Bar is expected to open in December at 2301 Corley Road in Cary. For more information, visit barobarnc.com. The globally celebrated Akira Back blends modern Japanese cuisine accented by bold Korean flavors in a refined and energetic atmosphere and will join two other yet-to-be-announced public-facing dining concepts. Perched on the hotel’s 10th floor with panoramic views of the St. Johns River and Downtown Jacksonville, the restaurant will bring Back’s inventive approach to Japanese cuisine to one of the city’s most prominent waterfront settings. The restaurant will be a signature component of the larger riverfront development, envisioned by Shanna Khan through Shanna Collective, which will bring Four Seasons hospitality, luxury residences and a collection of dining experiences to Jacksonville’s Shipyards. The project also includes a 170-key hotel and a connecting residential tower featuring 26 custom residences. Together, the hotel and residences will introduce a new expression of luxury hospitality and waterfront living to the city. “I am incredibly excited to bring my Akira Back restaurant to Jacksonville and collaborate with Four Seasons and Shanna Collective. It is an amazing opportunity to introduce the brand concept to this market which is constantly growing and evolving,” says Chef Akira Back. “With Jacksonville’s beautiful riverfront setting, we want to create a destination that brings people together in this community to share my contemporary interpretation of Japanese cuisine, shaped by my Korean and American heritage along with global culinary experiences from my travels around the world.” Chef Back has built an international following for menus that balance traditional Japanese techniques with unexpected ingredients and contemporary presentation. articles.title: Del Taco Brings Back Beef Birria
articles.titleKo: Del Taco Brings Back Beef Birria
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Shredded Beef Birria season is returning at Del Taco. Beginning Nov. 19, Del Taco, the nation’s second-largest Mexican quick service restaurant*, will bring back its acclaimed lineup of slow-braised Shredded Beef Birria favorites, including Street Tacos, a Grilled Combo Burrito, Quesadilla and award-winning Birria Ramen. Del Taco has now added Birria Loaded Fries to the Shredded Beef Birria lineup. “Shredded Beef Birria has become a strong and well-received seasonal platform for us because it delivers a flavor profile guests know and love while giving us the flexibility to evolve the menu around it,” said Noah Chillingworth, Chief Marketing Officer of Del Taco. “Balancing what guests want with finding new reasons for them to visit is central to Del Taco menu innovation, so we’re bringing back favorites, adding Loaded Fries and giving guests more ways to experience birria without sacrificing the preparation and flavors that originally made the lineup so successful.” Del Taco’s Shredded Beef Birria is braised for two and a half hours with traditional spices and chile peppers, resulting in tender, flavorful beef. Each item is served with a cup of savory consomé for dipping or drizzling. Guests can choose from several ways to enjoy the returning favorite, whether tucked into fresh grilled, cheese-crusted corn tortillas, served over crispy Crinkle Cut Fries, folded into a quesadilla, wrapped in a grilled burrito or served with wavy ramen noodles in a warm cup of consomé. The Shredded Beef Birria lineup includes: Shredded Beef Birria Street Tacos: These tacos start with fresh house-grated cheddar cheese, melted between two fresh grilled corn tortillas, filled with tender and savory shredded beef birria, topped with diced onions and chopped cilantro. Served with two fresh-cut lime wedges and a side of flavorful consomé for dipping. Shredded Beef Birria Grilled Combo Burrito: Tender and savory shredded beef birria, slow-cooked beans made from scratch, fresh house-grated cheddar cheese, tangy green sauce, diced onions and chopped cilantro, wrapped in a warm flour tortilla and flat-grilled to perfection. Served with a side of flavorful consomé for dipping. articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . Chef Rochelle Daniel, the two-time James Beard Award semifinalist behind MICHELIN-Recommended Atria, will open Pompette, an all-day French bistro and bakery, and Little Rich Girl (LRG), an underground speakeasy-style cocktail bar, in downtown Flagstaff on Dec. 15. Pompette sits next door to Atria, which Daniel opened in 2021, and LRG is tucked one floor below in the same century-old building. Together, the three restaurants give downtown Flagstaff three distinct dining experiences from one award-winning chef. OpenTable reservations are now available starting on opening day: Pompette and Little Rich Girl. “Atria was always the first piece of a bigger picture, and Pompette and Little Rich Girl are what complete it,” said Daniel. “Flagstaff has supported us from day one, and Atria’s recent MICHELIN recognition is bringing even more people to our city. We want them to find more ways to spend a day with us, from a morning croissant to a late-night cocktail and everything in between. There’s just nothing like this in Northern Arizona.” Mornings at Pompette start at the grab-and-go counter, stocked with fresh pastries and breads from Pastry Chef Alicia Motter, who has overseen the pastry program at Atria since the restaurant opened. Laminated doughs lead the offerings, including a Pistachio Cruffin, an Eggnog Custard Croissant and a Cinnamon Sugar Morning Bun, while breakfast staples like a Breakfast Burrito with egg, potato, bacon and cheddar round out the menu. By midday, the dining room shifts into lunch service with the lively, welcoming feel of a French bistro, offering options like a Lobster Roll with Old Bay and lemon aioli on a house-made brioche bun; Steak Frites with a flat iron steak, sauce au poivre and caramelized onions; Chicken Coq Au Vin; and Bouillabaisse with market fish, shrimp, mussels, saffron risotto, fennel and tomato nage. At dinner, Pompette leans into French-inspired classics executed with the precision and ingredient-first philosophy Daniel has become known for, plus meats prepared on a custom open-fire hearth. Favorites are sure to include Poulet Rôti with potato, dill and mustard velouté arriving as a half or whole bird; De Porc Au Miel, a roasted pork rack, balsamic honey glaze and pickles; Lumache, Duck Confit with black currant and Kale; and Fazzoletti Pasta, tossed with braised rabbit, Dijon, herbs and carrots, then finished with a carrot-top salsa verde. Later, the night moves downstairs to LRG, in a city with a documented history of underground drinking, secret tunnels and Prohibition-era contraband. The bar was conceived as a natural extension of that history, intimate, unhurried and serious about its craft. The cocktail program at LRG is led by Beverage Director Michael Hopper, who also oversees the bar at Pompette and Atria and was named Top Mixologist/Bartender by the 2025 Foodist Awards, the highest culinary honor in Arizona. Cocktails range from Good Intentions, made with gin, oolong tea syrup, marigold liqueur and egg white, to the Vaquero, which pairs reposado tequila with chocolate, orange, espresso and cinnamon and HeartBeet, with mezcal, chamomile-rosemary syrup, beet powder, walnut and egg white. Daniel brings her fine dining background to a menu that doesn’t take itself too seriously. Caviar service and Foie Gras Pâté sit alongside a Wagyu Linz Smash Burger with cheddar, bacon jam, gem lettuce, red onion and sauce marie rose on a potato bun, and the All Beef Glizzy, baked in fresh dough, comes one of two ways: with mustard, chives, Calabrian aioli and pepperoncini, or with melted cheddar, bacon and pickle. Dessert is just as playful, with a warm Cinnamon Roll iced tableside and an Ice Cream Sandwich. Located at 101 N. Leroux Street, Pompette serves fresh pastries, bread and grab-and-go from 7 to 11 a.m., lunch from 11 a.m. to 3 p.m. and dinner from 5 to 10 p.m. daily.

In that role, she oversaw brand strategy, creative, media, digital, loyalty, consumer insights and Guest engagement. Prior to that, Moss spent more than a decade on the agency side, developing brand strategies and integrated marketing campaigns for nationally recognized restaurants, including Domino’s and Jimmy John’s. A catering order might have just one name on the receipt, but think about everyone sitting around the table. How many of those people have never visited your restaurant? How many are experiencing your food for the first time? That’s what makes catering such an interesting opportunity for full-service restaurants. It’s a chance to introduce your brand to an entire room of new guests and earn their future visits—but that’s determined by if you get the experience right. Of course, that takes more than putting larger portions of your regular menu into aluminum trays. Food needs to travel well, and thoughtful packaging is a key piece of that puzzle. But the equation also includes your team members, who need clear processes and training to execute at a high level. Oh and also, none of this can come at the expense of the guests in your dining room. That’s why catering is such a challenge that many operators simply put off until they realize what an incredible revenue stream it can be, and then quickly scramble to find the answers to what makes a good catering program tick. In a recent webinar, FSR sat down with Jordan Johnson, director of off premise at Firebirds Wood Fired Grill, to learn how she built the structure behind the brand’s catering program that has successfully scaled across 70+ locations in 23 states. WATCH THE ENTIRE WEBINAR ON DEMAND HERE . When Johnson joined Firebirds in 2022, demand was already there. Guests were asking for catering, and operators were finding ways to accommodate them. The task was to turn that existing business into a consistent program that could work across the system. Jordan Johnson is Director of Off-Premise at Firebirds Wood Fired Grill, where she leads national catering and off-premise growth. Johnson unpacked the work behind that effort, from testing packaging in Charlotte to helping individual restaurants capture more business without overextending their kitchens. Here are five learnings from the webinar for full-service operators looking to build or strengthen their own catering playbooks. 1. Prove the demand, then build the infrastructure. Firebirds didn’t start with the question of whether guests wanted catering. Operators, sales data, reviews, and incoming inquiries had already supplied the answer. “Our goal was to hone in on that and make it a scalable program for us, a scalable channel for us,” Johnson says. For restaurants seeking leadership buy-in, she recommends documenting the business already knocking on the door: phone calls, emails, large orders, and sales generated without a formal catering system. Those requests can help make the case for dedicated resources. However, demand is only half the equation. Johnson also puts technology near the top of her catering launch checklist. Operators need to understand whether their ordering platforms and existing systems can support catering without creating a mountain of manual work. At Firebirds, that meant working through menu integration and getting orders to flow into the POS. The playbook also addresses what happens when an order doesn’t reach the system as intended. The takeaway: Start with evidence of what guests want and a clear understanding of what the restaurant can execute. The finer details of delivery settings and promotional assets can follow. 2. But Johnson knew a controlled environment couldn’t answer every operational question. Early in her tenure, she spent several months working at a restaurant to understand its off-premises flow. Birdcall – a Colorado-born fast casual brand known for its naturally superior chicken, innovative technology, and elevated guest experience – is headed to New Mexico after signing a multi-unit franchise agreement for three restaurants in Albuquerque. The development will be led by Naresh Patel and his company, AKSHAR QSR LLC. A veteran franchise operator with nearly 20 years of experience in the restaurant and hospitality industries, Patel’s portfolio includes ownership and operation of two Dairy Queen locations in Alabama, along with two franchised hotels, a Best Western in Alabama and a Comfort Inn in Truth or Consequences, New Mexico. While leases have yet to be signed, Patel is targeting a strategic northern expansion arc across the Albuquerque metro area, eyeing premier retail and commuter corridors in Northeast Albuquerque, the Cottonwood area, Rio Rancho, and Enchanted Hills. “Albuquerque represents an exciting opportunity for Birdcall, and we couldn’t be more pleased to have the right partners in place to bring our brand to the market,” said Justin Livingston, Vice President of Franchise Development for Birdcall. “This is a terrific ownership group that shares our vision for thoughtful growth, operational excellence and delivering an exceptional guest experience. We’re confident that together, we’ll build something special in Albuquerque and introduce the community to everything that makes Birdcall unique.” Patel added, “We’re excited to bring something fresh and exciting to the Albuquerque market. From the quality and creativity of the food to the energy of the restaurant experience, Birdcall is a brand that really stands out. We see tremendous opportunity in Albuquerque and look forward to introducing the community to Birdcall while building a strong presence in the market for years to come.” Each new restaurant will feature Birdcall’s signature atmosphere, combining modern design, vibrant artwork, family-friendly dining spaces, and convenient self-order kiosks designed to create a fast, seamless guest experience. The made-to-order menu features eight signature chicken sandwiches, hand-cut tenders, gluten-free nuggets, and chef-inspired salads—all made with all-natural chicken—alongside a variety of sides such as fries, tater tots, loaded tots, and slaws, complemented by hand-spun specialty milkshakes and an array of house-made sauces and dressings. Guests also enjoy draft beer and house-made margaritas, with Happy Hour specials. In addition to its culinary offerings, Birdcall emphasizes community engagement by supporting and partnering with local nonprofits and organizations. This includes meal donations, school partnerships, and fundraiser nights in which a portion of sales are donated back to participating organizations. The planned Albuquerque expansion is part of Birdcall’s broader national franchise initiative. The company currently operates 17 restaurants across Colorado, Arizona, Texas, and Mississippi, with at least 25 additional locations in various stages of development across Colorado, Idaho, Indiana, and now New Mexico. Bacio di Latte was founded in 2011 by brothers Edoardo and Luigi Tonolli, inspired by their shared passion for authentic Italian gelato. The brothers traveled from their hometown of Milan throughout Italy, sampling gelato, researching traditional techniques, and refining the art of gelato-making. Their journey shaped the signature recipes and artisanal approach that would come to define the brand. The journey began with a single storefront on Rua Oscar Freire, one of São Paulo’s most popular shopping streets. Since then, Bacio di Latte has grown into an international brand, expanding to more than 250 locations across Brazil and 30 in the United States, becoming the world’s largest artisanal gelato chain. Now, the brand is preparing to bring its signature Italian gelato to New York City’s West Village. Bacio di Latte makes its gelato fresh in-store every day, sourcing the best dairy from local farms and vendors, such as Hudson Valley Fresh for the high-quality milk, to using the freshest fruits and premium raw ingredients from around the world, like chocolate from Belgium to pistachio and hazelnuts from Italy. With more than 22 flavors to choose from, there’s something for everyone like iconic best sellers Chocolate Pistacchio Crunch, made with Italian-grown pistachios, Giandujotto, a decadent blend of hazelnut and Belgian chocolate; and Strawberry Cheesecake, featuring rich cheesecake gelato swirled with fresh strawberry jam. Crowd-pleasers like Crema & Biscotti, generously loaded with cookies, and Salted Caramel, a perfectly balanced blend of sweet and salty. For those seeking fruit-forward or non-dairy options, Fragola Sorbet delivers a light, vibrant burst of fresh strawberry flavor, while Buttercream Pretzel offers a distinctive combination of pretzel-flavored gelato and buttery pretzel cream. Bacio di Latte introduces rotating seasonal specialties throughout the year, inviting guests to discover new and unexpected flavors. Among them will be Big Apple Crumble, in celebration of their first NYC location, featuring creamy mascarpone and vanilla gelato swirled with apple compote and cinnamon, finished with a sweet crumble topping. For guests interested in experiencing all that Bacio di Latte has to offer, a signature upgrade, featuring cups and waffle cones coated in hazelnut and pistachio spreads, as well as a fresh baked Cookie Collection. Plus, the classic Bacio Affogato Bar bringing together two Italian passions, gelato and espresso coffee. Exclusive New York menu items include Tiramisu Affogato, Chocolate Chip Cookie Affogato, and Bacio Hot Chocolate. The shop’s interior is designed like a cozy Italian country kitchen with hand glazed tile, exposed wood beams, and extensive millwork enveloped in a signature white paint reminiscent of gelato’s most important ingredient: milk, which Bacio di Latte sources from Hudson Valley Fresh, a farmer-owned dairy cooperative known for its high-quality. Throughout the space, shelves (accessed by a charming rolling library ladder) are filled with milk bottles, latte cups, copper bowls, whisks, and other cooking tools, further reinforcing the brand’s dedication to its craft. The guest experience at each location features a dedicated playlist for each portion of the day, from Dean Martin, Madeleine Peyroux, and other jazz variants in the morning, to French bossa nova in the afternoon and electrotango in the evening. articles.title: Economia circular movimenta até R$ 90,7 bilhões no Brasil
articles.titleKo: Economia circular movimenta até R$ 90,7 bilhões no Brasil
articles.originalSummary: A economia circular movimenta entre R$ 31 bilhões e R$ 90,7 bilhões no Brasil, segundo levantamento inédito da Confederação Nacional da Indústria ( CNI ). Apresentado na 31ª Conferência das Nações Unidas sobre Mudança do Clima (COP31), em Antália, na Turquia, o estudo Financiamento para a Economia Circular na Indústria Brasileira, mostra que o país tem um mercado de finanças sustentáveis estimado em R$ 884 bilhões. Segundo a CNI, os recursos destinados diretamente à circularidade representam entre 3,5% e 10,3% desse total. O percentual é superior à média mundial, de aproximadamente 2%. Apesar do volume de investimentos, a pesquisa identifica um desequilíbrio na distribuição dos recursos. A maior parte do dinheiro está concentrada em iniciativas de reciclagem, gestão de resíduos e recuperação de materiais, enquanto projetos voltados à prevenção do desperdício, ao desenvolvimento de produtos sustentáveis e ao reaproveitamento de insumos recebem uma parcela menor. O que é economia circular? Diferentemente do modelo tradicional de produção e consumo, conhecido como economia linear, a economia circular busca manter materiais e produtos em uso pelo maior tempo possível. Na economia linear, o modelo é baseado na extração de recursos naturais, fabricação, consumo e descarte. A economia circular propõe reduzir a extração de matérias-primas, evitar a geração de resíduos e aproveitar melhor os recursos naturais em todas as etapas da cadeia produtiva. Na prática, o modelo envolve iniciativas como: Design sustentável: desenvolver produtos que usem menos matéria-prima e sejam mais duráveis; Reutilização: dar novas aplicações a produtos e materiais que ainda podem ser aproveitados; Reparo: recuperar equipamentos e produtos para prolongar sua vida útil; Reciclagem: transformar resíduos em matéria-prima para novos processos produtivos; Eficiência de insumos: reduzir o desperdício de água, energia e materiais durante a fabricação. O sistema pretende fazer com que os recursos permaneçam circulando na economia, reduzindo impactos ambientais e os custos da atividade industrial. Recursos concentrados De acordo com o levantamento da CNI, 80,8% dos recursos identificados para a economia circular são destinados exclusivamente à gestão de resíduos, reciclagem e recuperação de materiais no fim da vida útil dos produtos. As etapas anteriores à geração de resíduos, que envolvem mudanças no desenvolvimento e na fabricação dos produtos, recebem uma parcela significativamente menor dos investimentos. O estudo identificou a seguinte distribuição: 80,8%: gestão de resíduos, reciclagem e recuperação de materiais; 11,5%: reutilização, reparo e extensão da vida útil de produtos e ativos; 7,7%: design sustentável, prevenção de resíduos e eficiência no uso de insumos. Segundo os números, embora a reciclagem seja importante, a economia circular depende de mudanças em toda a cadeia produtiva, desde a concepção dos produtos até sua destinação final. Como financiar a circularidade Em nota, o superintendente de Meio Ambiente e Sustentabilidade da CNI, Davi Bomtempo, destacou que a economia circular representa uma oportunidade para reduzir custos operacionais e emissões de gases de efeito estufa na indústria de transformação. Segundo ele, as empresas interessadas em financiar projetos sustentáveis podem recorrer a diferentes instrumentos, como linhas de crédito de bancos públicos e privados, emissão de títulos verdes no mercado de capitais e participação em editais e chamadas públicas de fomento. Entre as modalidades identificadas pela pesquisa, estão: Empréstimos verdes (Green Loans): representam 27,9% das operações mapeadas; Capital de risco (Equity/VC/PE): corresponde a 20,9%; Financiamento combinado (Blended Finance): responde por 16,3%. Desafios para avançar O levantamento também aponta fatores que dificultam a ampliação dos investimentos em economia circular. Para Bomtempo, um dos problemas é a dificuldade de identificar e classificar essas iniciativas dentro do me

Wendy’s is serving up holiday cheer with the Peppermint Frosty Swirl and Peppermint Brownie Frosty Fusion, available now for a limited time. The holidays move fast. Between packed calendars, growing to-do lists and the rush to make every moment count, sometimes the best gift is simply a reason to slow down. This holiday season, Wendy’s is serving up exactly that by honoring a beloved piece of its heritage: the iconic glass-walled Solarium. For years, Wendy’s fans have reminisced about the Solariums, sharing memories and photos of time spent enjoying a meal, reading magazines, playing games and simply enjoying what was right in front of them. Now, Wendy’s is bringing that feeling back, giving fans a chance to relive some of their fondest memories. Beginning today, Wendy’s Holiday Box is available at participating restaurants nationwide for a limited time. Starting at $11.99,* the meal is served in Solarium-inspired packaging and includes a Dave’s Double made with fresh, never frozen beef** or 10-piece Crispy or Spicy Chicken Nuggets, with small Hot & Crispy Fries, a small soft drink and one of four collectible retro knit hats. And because no holiday meal is complete without a little something to unwrap, the hat comes tucked inside a holiday-themed blind bag, keeping the design a surprise until the big reveal. The retro designs celebrate “Frosty”, “Where’s the Beef?”, “Biggie” and Wendy’s, making all four worth unwrapping and collecting for this year’s holiday card photoshoot. “For our fans, the sunroom was a place where memories were made over a meal together, and that feels especially relevant during the holiday rush,” said Tariq Hassan, Chief Marketing & Customer Growth Officer, Wendy’s. “We’re bringing that feeling back, from a real Solarium in New York City to a Holiday Meal fans can enjoy anywhere. So, pull up a seat, enjoy a hot, juicy cheeseburger, throw on a warm Wendy’s hat and spend a little more time together.” Your Childhood Wendy’s Is Home for the Holidays The love and connection for the Solarium runs deep with fans. Beginning in the 1980s, the glass-walled dining rooms became more than a distinctive part of Wendy’s restaurant design. For fans who grew up with Wendy’s Solariums, the memories have stuck. Glimpses of the iconic glass-walled sunrooms on social media still transport them back to childhood and the moments they shared there. For younger fans discovering the Solarium for the first time, it offers something equally meaningful – a chance to slow down, connect in real life and discover a piece of Wendy’s history along the way. That’s why, on Nov. 17 and 18, Wendy’s is turning those memories into something fans can experience again with a limited-time holiday Solarium pop-up in New York City’s Flatiron District. For two days only, fans can step away from the holiday rush and into a classic, cozy Wendy’s Solarium decked out in its holiday best, complete with Holiday Meals and plenty of nods to Wendy’s heritage. Whether fans remember the original or are discovering the Solarium for the first time, Wendy’s is creating a place to sit back, settle in and make a new holiday memory. More Ways to Celebrate, the Wendy’s Way And because one holiday miracle wasn’t enough, Wendy’s is spreading even more cheer this season from festive spins on menu favorites to gifts that keep on giving, and quality food at a price that helps holiday budgets go further. Peppermint Meets Frosty: Starting today, Wendy’s is bringing one of the season’s signature flavors to its iconic frozen treat with two peppermint Frosty creations. The Peppermint Frosty Swirl combines Wendy’s classic Vanilla or Chocolate Frosty with a swirl of peppermint sauce, while the Peppermint Brownie Frosty Fusion takes things up a notch, adding rich brownie pieces for an extra-indulgent holiday treat. ‘Tis the Season for Frosty Key Tags: For only

articles.title: Ri Happy estreia na Shopee e amplia presença em marketplaces
articles.titleKo: Ri Happy estreia na Shopee e amplia presença em marketplaces
articles.originalSummary: O Grupo Ri Happy estreia na seção de Lojas Oficiais da Shopee, espaço dedicado a grandes marcas, e passa a atuar em marketplaces. A iniciativa integra a estratégia de transformação operacional conduzida pela nova gestão , que tem entre as prioridades a otimização dos canais físicos e digitais, a melhoria da experiência de compra e o fortalecimento de parcerias. Com produtos de diferentes categorias do universo infantil e entregas para todo o Brasil, a loja oficial amplia o acesso ao portfólio da Ri Happy em um momento estratégico para o varejo, às vésperas da Black Friday e do Natal, principal período de vendas do setor de brinquedos. A entrada na plataforma combina a presença de uma marca com mais de 35 anos de história à audiência e à estrutura da Shopee. A parceria permite à companhia alcançar consumidores em diferentes regiões e complementar sua atuação nas lojas físicas e no e-commerce próprio. O movimento acompanha a mudança nos hábitos de compra das famílias brasileiras, que transitam entre diferentes canais. Ao diversificar os pontos de contato com os consumidores, a Ri Happy busca oferecer uma jornada de compra mais conveniente e integrada, além de avançar na eficiência da operação digital. “Estamos conduzindo uma transformação que coloca o cliente e as parcerias no centro das nossas decisões. A chegada à Shopee materializa essa estratégia ao ampliar nossa presença digital, fortalecer nossos canais de venda e criar novas oportunidades de conexão com as famílias brasileiras”, afirma Carlos Fernandes, COO do Grupo Ri Happy. Ele complementa: “Queremos combinar a tradição e a força da Ri Happy com modelos de operação cada vez mais eficientes, competitivos e alinhados à forma como as pessoas compram hoje. Essa parceria é um passo importante nessa direção.” A parceria também abre espaço para iniciativas de relacionamento e engajamento por meio do ecossistema de social commerce da Shopee, que inclui Shopee Live, Shopee Vídeo e Programa de Criadores. A Ri Happy poderá explorar formatos interativos de apresentação de produtos e ampliar a visibilidade de seu portfólio. “A chegada da Ri Happy, uma empresa tão presente no imaginário brasileiro, reafirma o papel da Shopee como parceira estratégica dos vendedores da plataforma. Esse movimento reforça a Shopee como o principal destino de compras para milhões de brasileiros, conectando o público às suas marcas favoritas”, afirma Felipe Lima, diretor de Desenvolvimento de Negócios e Operações Fulfillment da Shopee. A entrada na Shopee é o primeiro movimento de uma estratégia mais ampla de atuação em marketplaces, que deverá ter novos desdobramentos nos próximos meses. A iniciativa faz parte dos esforços do Grupo Ri Happy para fortalecer sua competitividade e preparar a companhia para um novo ciclo de desenvolvimento. articles.title: Swig Accelerates Expansion in Q3
articles.titleKo: Swig Accelerates Expansion in Q3
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Swig, the Home of the Original Dirty Soda and category-creating beverage brand, accelerated its national expansion throughout the third quarter of 2026, celebrating 13 grand openings across eight states and announcing four new development agreements. As dirty soda continues to dominate mainstream popularity, Swig remains at the forefront of the growing beverage category through strategic development, menu innovation, and a loyal customer following. During Q3, Swig opened new locations across Illinois, Idaho, Texas, Tennessee, Florida, Arizona, South Carolina, and Nevada, bringing its customizable beverages to more communities nationwide. Likewise, signed agreements highlighted new markets including South Denver, Chicago, Washington and Boston. With more than 450 total franchise location commitments to date, the brand continues to expand its development pipeline and establish a presence in new territories through 2027. “Throughout the third quarter, we made significant strides in bringing Swig to more communities while continuing to strengthen our position as the leader in the dirty soda category,” said Alex Dunn, CEO of Swig. “Our momentum shows the strength of our franchise model, the dedication of our operators, and the loyal guests who continue to embrace the Swig experience. As we look ahead, we’re focused on building on this progress and introducing even more communities to what makes Swig unique.” Alongside its development achievements, Swig continued to innovate its menu with new offerings and returning fan favorites. The brand introduced Swig Energy as a new drink base, expanding its customizable beverage options, and brought back its popular Garlic Parmesan Pretzel Bites for a limited time. Swig also welcomed the return of its seasonal favorites, Spice Spice Baby and Autumn Blush, while debuting two new fall limited-time offerings, Caramel Apple and Pumpkin Chocolate Chip Cookie. Beyond menu innovation, Swig continued its commitment to giving back through its seventh annual Save the Cups campaign, which provides financial assistance to women battling breast cancer and promotes early detection. The initiative encourages guests to support the cause through purchases of select menu items, limited-edition merchandise, and donations at checkout. This year’s campaign raised more than $650,000, furthering Swig’s mission to ease the financial burden of breast cancer treatment for women and families nationwide. With a growing development pipeline, a steady pace of new openings and continued menu innovation, Swig enters the final quarter of 2026 with strong momentum. The brand remains focused on expanding into new territories, supporting its franchise partners and introducing its signature dirty soda experience to more communities across the United States. Some of Grill 23’s younger guests first came in for a martini photo. Then they stayed for dinner. For Chris Himmel, CEO of Himmel Hospitality Group, that progression is an encouraging sign for the Boston steakhouse, which opened in 1983. Alongside regulars in their 50s, 60s, and 70s, he’s seeing diners in their 20s and early 30s discover the restaurant. “They started by coming in just to go get a picture with a martini with ice chips on it, and now they’re realizing that they can stay for dinner,” Himmel says. The steakhouse atmosphere is having a moment, he acknowledges. But keeping Grill 23 relevant has involved decades of reinvestment, menu decisions, and attention to the people delivering the experience. On FSR’s Restaurant Innovator podcast, Himmel and chef-partner Robert Sisca discussed how they approach that work as national restaurant groups expand in Boston and Himmel Hospitality prepares to open two restaurants in 2027. Grill 23 began as a single-floor, 185-seat steakhouse founded by Himmel’s father, Ken. Its early menu offered just a few steak options. As the business grew, leadership regularly stopped to examine what could improve the experience. “They reassessed every three to five years,” Himmel says. That process helped shape investments in the wine program and culinary talent, at a time when an ambitious chef might not have viewed a steakhouse as an obvious career destination. Today, Sisca brings a fine-dining background that includes nearly five years at Le Bernardin. He oversees the group’s four existing concepts, each with its own identity and dishes guests expect to find. At Grill 23, some steaks have been on the menu for 43 years. At the group’s French bistro, the bouillabaisse has endured for 17. Those dishes aren’t going away, Sisca says, although their preparation or presentation may evolve. He wants chefs to recognize what brings people back before deciding what needs updating. “A lot of people do look for signatures,” he says. “They do look for cocktails and dishes that make you want to come back.” That doesn’t mean leaving a restaurant untouched. Sisca believes operators need to reassess their concepts and avoid falling into the routine of doing the same thing simply because they always have. But novelty alone isn’t a reason to change. “I don’t always love to just follow the trends because trends die,” he says. “Good hospitality and good food lasts forever.” Delivering that consistently has become an increasingly demanding assignment at Grill 23. Himmel says an 800-cover, $100,000 night once occurred only a handful of times. Now, he describes that level of business as happening almost nightly. At roughly 150–160 per person, volume doesn’t buy the team any forgiveness. “The expectations don’t waver compared to a smaller restaurant,” he says. Long-serving employees help meet those expectations. Some servers have worked at Grill 23 for its entire 43-year history. More recently, employees’ children have joined the restaurants as hosts during school breaks and the holidays. Himmel, who previously worked for Danny Meyer, says he devotes as much attention to employee satisfaction as guest satisfaction. Hiring means looking beyond technical proficiency to consider someone’s attitude and effect on the team. The group has also been working to improve benefits, including retirement plans and vacation offerings. That investment matters when a dining room is full of people measuring tonight’s visit against years of previous meals—or deciding whether their first dinner deserves a return trip. articles.titleKo: Mania de Churrasco prepara expansão da rede no Brasil com restaurantes e lojas box em 2027
articles.originalSummary: O Mania de Churrasco! vai acelerar a abertura de restaurantes casuais e lojas box em 2027. O plano prevê consolidar a presença da marca nas regiões Sudeste, Sul, Centro-Oeste e Nordeste, unindo mercados onde a rede já atua com a expansão para novas localidades. “Nosso plano para 2027 é crescer de forma consistente, respeitando as particularidades de cada mercado e buscando oportunidades que façam sentido para o negócio e para os nossos franqueados. Queremos fortalecer nossa presença onde já atuamos e avançar em regiões com potencial para receber a marca”, afirma Filliphe Camelo, diretor do Mania de Churrasco!. A escolha dos pontos comerciais e dos formatos de operação leva em conta fatores como densidade populacional, renda, fluxo de pessoas e veículos e hábitos de consumo fora do lar. A análise ajuda a avaliar o potencial de cada região e definir o modelo mais adequado. Enquanto o restaurante casual é voltado a refeições completas, as unidades box são instaladas em locais de grande circulação, como praças de alimentação e centros comerciais. A expansão segue uma lógica em espiral, com prioridade para o fortalecimento da presença regional antes da entrada em novas praças. O modelo permite aproveitar o conhecimento dos mercados em que a rede já atua e identificar oportunidades em cidades próximas e em outras regiões do País. Atualmente, a rede tem 115 unidades em operação e uma em implantação. Programas de capacitação A rede investe na capacitação dos próprios funcionários, muitos deles em seu primeiro emprego. Cerca de 95% dos colaboradores atuam nas operações das lojas. “Nossa empresa é, acima de tudo, uma plataforma de desenvolvimento. Nossa missão é que todo colaborador saia daqui melhor do que entrou, com mais repertório, mais disciplina, mais conhecimento e valores sólidos que levará para a vida”, afirma Thiago Camelo de Souza, sócio e diretor da área de Gente da marca. Entre as iniciativas de capacitação e reconhecimento está o programa “Mania de Reconhecer”, que concede pontos aos funcionários conforme o desempenho. A pontuação pode ser trocada por prêmios, viagens e experiências. A rede mantém ainda o Programa de Liderança em Foco, treinamentos presenciais e on-line, encontros de gerentes e franqueados e uma convenção anual. articles.title: Buffalo Wild Wings GO to Debut in north Reno Plaza
articles.titleKo: Buffalo Wild Wings GO to Debut in north Reno Plaza
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Buffalo Wild Wings GO is giving Reno residents another way to satisfy their wing cravings starting Saturday, Nov. 21, as the brand debuts in North Reno Plaza — introducing a fast, convenient destination built around the brand’s legendary wings, signature sauces and crowd-pleasing shareables. Positioned at 1901 Silverada Blvd., the concept is owned and operated by franchisee Mayer Zahid, marking his second Buffalo Wild Wings GO in the Reno market. The launch follows his Virginia Street store earlier this spring, with an additional site slated to open next summer. Zahid brings over two decades of industry experience, including operating El Pollo Loco and Blaze Pizza locations. Grand opening day kicks off at 11 a.m., when the first 75 guests in line, ages 18 and older, will receive FREE wings for a year.* All guests who visit on Nov. 21 can also enjoy six free wings with any purchase all day. The restaurant will also offer a range of bundled options designed for easy group ordering, including wing-and-fries bundles and the Pick 6 Meal starting at $19.99, featuring customizable entrées, two sides and two fountain drinks. “Our family has been part of the Reno community for more than 20 years, and we’ve seen the rising demand for reliable, high-quality takeout food that fits into people’s busy, day-to-day routines,” said Zahid. “Buffalo Wild Wings GO gives guests meals that they know and love, with an experience that’s quick, consistent and built around convenience. It’s a natural fit as we continue to grow throughout the Silver State.” The new location features a menu centered on the brand’s most beloved items, including traditional and boneless wings, chicken dippers, burgers and sandwiches, as well as a lineup of 26 bold sauces and dry rubs. articles.title: Tips for Risk Reduction in Seasonal Restaurant Hiring
articles.titleKo: Tips for Risk Reduction in Seasonal Restaurant Hiring
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . When hiring, the general rule is hire slow and fire fast. As your business ramps up for the holiday, and you may feel the urge to hire quickly, please consider these tips to keep the risks of seasonal hiring as low as they can be. BE CAREFUL OF AI USE, INCLUDING AUTOMATED HIRING TOOLS, IN HIRING So many employers are using AI now, especially to screen resumes and assist with hiring decisions. However, doing so is risky, in that AI may screen out candidates for improper reasons, including legally protected categories. Using AI without human oversight can expose an employer to unnecessary risks. Tip: Keep the “human” part of human resources in place, even with seasonal hiring screening. JUST BECAUSE SOMEONE IS SEASONAL, OR TEMPORARY, DOES NOT MAKE THEM A VIABLE INDEPENDENT CONTRACTOR Common sense might suggest that a short-term or temporary worker can simply be paid as a contract worker, by 1099. Better for them and better for the employer, right? Wrong! Many states (California, Massachusetts and New Jersey) have strict tests about who can be an independent contractor. California follows the ABC test which requires: (A) the worker to be free from the employer’s control and direction in doing the work; (B) the work must be outside the employer’s usual course of business; and (C) the worker must be customarily engaged in an independently established trade, occupation or business (of the same type as the work being performed). Many seasonal hires won’t meet any prong of this test, let alone all three. So, the test won’t be met in states that don’t include the “usual course of business” requirement (Colorado, Pennsylvania, and Wisconsin). Misclassifying seasonal workers can lead to class claims for wage-and-hour violations, back taxes, penalties, and a host of other risks. Tip: Resist the urge to hire seasonal workers as contractors. STAFFING COMPANY CONSIDERATIONS Some staffing companies are terrific, and provide excellent workers quickly, who are well worth the premium you pay for them. Other staffing companies are less terrific, may not vet their workers thoroughly, pay them properly, or indemnify you (as the customer) for their glitches. Too many of my clients have gotten stuck paying for mistakes made by the staffing companies (as the alleged joint employer). Tip: Vet your staffing companies, read the agreements carefully, and understand the benefit you are getting for the premium you are paying. ONBOARD SEASONAL WORKERS PROPERLY Often employers don’t take the special care they need for seasonal workers to make sure they sign off on all of the proper new hire paperwork. Any offers to seasonal employees should clarify that the work is temporary (or seasonal), and expected to end in January 2027. This can help limit unemployment claims and set clear worker expectations. If seasonal employees are not entitled to certain benefits, like vacation time, or paid holidays, be clear about that up front. Also, seasonal workers should sign your arbitration agreement, your handbook, and should get all required notices (like California’s “Know Your Rights Notice” ) just like your regular full-time employees do. If you conduct new hire training on your policies, such as harassment prevention, or wage-and-hour compliance, proper timekeeping, etc., train your seasonal hires too. Tip: Remember, seasonal workers are less vested given their short tenure, and be more likely to take advantage of compliance oversights. WATCH THOSE LOCAL MINIMUM WAGE INCREASES While many states have minimum wage increases as of January 1each year, some cities and counties raise their own minimum wages on July 1 (in 2026, rates increased in several cities and counties in California, Illinois, Maryland and Minnesota). In California, there were even industry-specific minimum wage hikes in July 2026, so beware. Tip: Make sure you are hiring seasonal wo

articles.title: Black Angus Steakhouse Opens First Takeout-Only Location
articles.titleKo: Black Angus Steakhouse Opens First Takeout-Only Location
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . Black Angus Steakhouse is introducing a new way to experience the iconic brand and its 21-day-aged steaks, with its first-ever late-night takeout-only location, opening in Echo Park. The move builds on Black Angus’ longstanding commitment to quality, value, and memorable dining experiences, while expanding beyond its traditional restaurant model to serve a new Los Angeles community. Beginning November 16th and operating daily from 11 a.m. to 11 p.m., the Echo Park menu will feature customer favorites from the steakhouse as well as its Bad A** Steakhouse Burgers concept and raw meat Black Angus Market. Customers will find offerings such as the signature Campfire Feast Dinner For Two, Porterhouse Steak, BBQ Baby Back Ribs, and Grilled Salmon, as well as Bad A** Burgers’ Original Outlaw Cheeseburger and Rodeo Ripper Bacon Cheeseburger stacked with onion rings. Desserts and group ordering options will also be available. Orders will be available through Black Angus’ and Bad A** Steakhouse Burgers’ Echo Park sites for pickup, delivery within a 10-mile radius, or through DoorDash, Uber Eats, and Grubhub. Echo Park boasts late-night hours, being the first location open until 11 p.m. Founded in 1964 by American cattle rancher Stewart Anderson, Black Angus was built on the belief that classic steakhouse dining should be accessible and affordable without compromising quality. That philosophy continues to guide the brand today, from its 21-day-aged steaks grilled over an open flame to its scratch-made sides and sauces made in each restaurant kitchen. The Echo Park location represents a new way to bring the Black Angus experience to customers, adapting the brand’s service model to meet evolving dining habits. Black Angus has continued to explore new ways to serve customers. In 2022 the brand expanded with the Black Angus Market butcher shop concept, offering premium cuts of raw meat for pickup and shipment nationwide. Bad A** Steakhouse Burgers was started as a delivery-only concept in 2023, opening up the steakhouse-style burgers to new combinations such as a mushroom & bleu cheese burger. The Echo Park location builds on this evolution, bringing the brand’s offerings to a more urban market through the takeout-only format. “It’s always exciting to introduce a new way for guests to enjoy Black Angus and connect with a new audience,” said Deborah Shapiro, Vice President of Growth at Black Angus Steakhouse. “We are committed to growing and evolving with our customers, and this new takeout location is another way to reach our communities where they are.” The post Black Angus Steakhouse Opens First Takeout-Only Location appeared first on FSR magazine .

articles.title: Marcas próprias avançam em categorias básicas e crescem 36% nos supermercados
articles.titleKo: Marcas próprias avançam em categorias básicas e crescem 36% nos supermercados
articles.originalSummary: Em tempos de orçamento apertado, os produtos de marca própria ganham espaço como alternativa para consumidores que buscam economizar nas compras do supermercado. A participação desses produtos no faturamento dos supermercados cresceu 28% em setembro, em relação ao mesmo período de 2025. De janeiro a setembro, a alta acumulada foi de 36%. A expansão, no entanto, ocorre de maneira diferente entre as regiões e os segmentos de produtos. Enquanto no Sudeste os produtos de marca própria respondem por 5% das vendas da cesta básica, no Nordeste a participação é de apenas 0,8%. A diferença aparece em categorias como feijão e papel higiênico e reflete também as particularidades do consumo em cada mercado. No Nordeste, marcas regionais de feijão, arroz, café e farinha têm forte presença nas compras dos consumidores. A preferência por esses produtos, muitos deles ligados aos hábitos locais, ajuda a explicar por que as marcas próprias ainda têm menor participação nas categorias básicas da alimentação. Na região, elas encontram mais espaço em ovos, produtos de limpeza e mercearia. No Sudeste, a presença é maior justamente nos itens básicos. O feijão de marca própria, por exemplo, representa 17,6% das vendas da categoria, contra 2,8% no Nordeste. Em papel higiênico, a diferença também é expressiva: 17% ante 3,3%. A distância entre as regiões é menor quando considerados os produtos embalados em geral. Nesse grupo, as marcas próprias representam 3,8% das vendas no Sudeste e 3% no Nordeste. Imagem: Envato O post Marcas próprias avançam em categorias básicas e crescem 36% nos supermercados apareceu primeiro em Mercado&Consumo .
