articles.title: Handel’s Celebrates 200th Opening in Camarillo, California
articles.titleKo: Handel’s Celebrates 200th Opening in Camarillo, California
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Handel’s Ice Cream, the fastest-growing ice cream franchise in the nation, will celebrate the opening of its 200th location in Camarillo, California, on Nov. 12. The milestone comes during a record year of expansion for the 81-year-old ice cream brand, which has opened more new parlors in 2026 than in any previous year. Despite persistent inflation and uncertain consumer confidence, Handel’s continues to grow through major multi-unit development agreements and reinvestment from existing franchise owners. The brand attributes that growth in part to its unit-level economics, which rank among the strongest in the sweet treats category. “We’re thrilled to be opening our 200th location during such an incredible year for Handel’s,” said Jennifer Schuler, CEO of Handel’s Ice Cream. “Against a backdrop of persistent inflation, consumer price sensitivity and economic uncertainty, Handel’s is incredibly resilient and, in fact, even thrives in this type of environment. We keep it simple: ice cream made fresh in every store, served in generous portions at affordable prices. We want to be the kind of place where guests experience the opposite of shrinkflation. It’s a model that works for our guests and our franchise partners, as demonstrated by our 11 years of systemwide same-store sales growth.” The Camarillo opening marks the third Handel’s location for franchisees Scott and Vanessa Sonnenberg, who also operate parlors in Stevenson Ranch and Sand Canyon. It also expands Handel’s footprint in California, where the brand now has 70 parlors. The Sonnenbergs have another location planned for Simi Valley in 2027. “We’re incredibly proud to be opening Handel’s 200th location and celebrating this milestone with such a great brand,” said Scott Sonnenberg. “Handel’s has been an important part of our family’s journey, and the strength of the business model has given us the confidence to expand our ownership to multiple locations, with plans for more in the future. We’re excited to become a lasting part of the Camarillo community.” Strong Unit-Level Economics Fuel Record Franchise Development in 2026 As economic uncertainty and consumer spending pressures continue to challenge businesses across the country, Handel’s Homemade Ice Cream is proving that growth is possible with the right brand, business model and franchise partners. From January through November 2026, Handel’s has signed agreements for 75 new units, a record for the brand. Handel’s has now signed more commitments for new units in 2026 than the number of units signed during all of 2025. The majority of the agreements signed have been with multi-unit operators who are bringing Handel’s into new markets, including Chicago, while existing franchise owners continue to reinvest in the brand. While signings are the strongest in company history, Handel’s continues to set company records for new openings as well. The brand looks to open 35 new parlors by year-end and has broken into new states such as Florida, Idaho and Washington. The interest from new and existing franchisees comes as Handel’s continues to deliver strong unit-level performance. The brand reported an average unit volume of $1.1 million in 2025* and parlor-level EBITDA of 20.3% in 2024** and is currently in its 11th consecutive year of systemwide same-store sales growth. “With a 20% EBITDA margin, the unit economics are best in class for restaurant operations and make for an incredibly compelling investment,” said Erin Snyder, vice president of franchise development at Handel’s Ice Cream. “That, combined with a strong history, simple operations and whitespace to grow, makes Handel’s an attractive growth proposition for multi-unit operators. Handmade daily, the tamales are available individually, by the half-dozen or by the dozen. Just in time for the holiday season, Tocaya is bringing back its fan-favorite tamales, including the return of Sweet Corn Tamales and the debut of a new Chicken Verde variety. Available now for a limited time, the seasonal lineup gives guests two ways to enjoy the holiday staple. Handmade daily, the tamales are available individually, by the half-dozen or by the dozen, making them an easy addition to holiday gatherings, family dinners and group celebrations. A limited-time Kids Meal featuring tamales rounds out the seasonal lineup, offering something for the whole family. Piada Italian Street Food, a leading fast-casual Italian restaurant concept, is bringing a new twist to comfort food with the launch of Macdaddy’s Chicken Parm Mac, a limited-time menu collaboration with viral food creator Stefan Johnson, better known as “Snackdaddy.” The collaboration brings together Stefan’s larger-than-life personality and love of indulgent food with Piada’s Italian-inspired menu, combining two comfort food classics into one crave-worthy creation. Announced via social media on Instagram and TikTok, Macdaddy is available exclusively through Piada’s website and Piada One app at participating locations from November 9 through February 15, 2027, the launch brings a fresh approach to menu innovation for the growing fast-casual brand. Macdaddy’s Chicken Parm Mac features Piada’s creamy mac and cheese piled high with crispy chicken, marinara, creamy parmesan sauce and a finishing touch of parmesan cheese. The limited-time bowl puts an Italian spin on a comfort food favorite, delivering the cheesy, saucy flavors of chicken parmesan in every bite. Known for his unmistakable voice, entertaining food reviews and infectious enthusiasm, Stefan is a voice and on-screen actor that has built a loyal following, known as s_johnson_voiceovers across Instagram and TikTok, where his personality and passion for food have made him a recognizable voice in the digital food community. “I’m all about food that’s big on flavor, and when Piada gave me the chance to create my own mac and cheese bowl, I knew we had to take it to the next level,” said Stefan Johnson, known as Snackdaddy. “Chicken parm and mac and cheese are two of my favorite comfort foods, so bringing them together just made sense. It’s cheesy, saucy, crispy and everything you want in one bowl. I can’t wait for everyone to try it!” For Piada, the collaboration represents an opportunity to introduce the brand to new audiences while building on its digital-first menu strategy. By partnering with a creator whose content resonates with food lovers, Piada is bringing a fresh perspective to its mac and cheese platform while giving guests a limited-time reason to explore its digital ordering channels. “At Piada, we’re always looking for new ways to bring bold flavors and creativity to our menu, and partnering with Stefan was a natural fit,” said Matt Harding, Chief Culinary Officer of Piada Italian Street Food. “His enthusiasm for food is contagious, and we wanted to create something that reflects that energy while staying true to what we do best. Macdaddy’s Chicken Parm Mac brings together two comfort food favorites in a fun, indulgent way, and we’re excited for guests to experience it.” To celebrate the launch, Stefan will share exclusive content across Instagram and TikTok, giving followers a closer look at his signature creation and encouraging fans to experience the dish for themselves. Piada will also bring the collaboration to life across its digital channels, including its website, social media and Piada One loyalty app, where guests can unlock a limited-time Snackdaddy badge. Piada One members who order Macdaddy’s Chicken Parm Mac will also unlock an exclusive, limited-time MacDaddy Badge, a digital reward celebrating the collaboration and giving fans another reason to try Stefan’s signature creation. Macdaddy’s Chicken Parm Mac is available for four weeks only, November 9 through February 15, 2027, exclusively through mypiada.com and the Piada One app at participating Piada locations. A line of 20 to 30 cars should have been a welcome sight for Dillas Quesadillas founder Kyle Gordon. Instead, it became a warning that his growing chain had a serious problem. Gordon was standing outside one of Dillas’ newest restaurants in the Dallas-Fort Worth area, watching customers arrive during what initially seemed like a promising opening day. The drive-thru line kept growing, but the first car wasn’t moving. When he walked inside to investigate, he discovered an operation struggling to keep up with demand. Employees were overwhelmed, preparation tasks were unfinished, and the shift leader looked terrified. This wasn’t an inexperienced team, either. Several employees had spent eight to 10 weeks training at established Dillas restaurants because construction and signage delays had pushed back the opening. The restaurant eventually recorded approximately $15,000 in sales that day and between $70,000 and $75,000 during its opening week. Those numbers should have been cause for celebration. Gordon saw something else. Dillas had ambitions of becoming a chain capable of producing $3 million to $4 million in average unit volumes. If a restaurant couldn’t handle the demand it was already attracting, expanding the concept would only multiply its problems. “My goal at Dillas, our goal, is to do this every single day,” Gordon says. The experience became a turning point for the Texas-based quesadilla chain. The brand didn’t accelerate expansion. Gordon made the difficult decision to pause development and rebuild the business from the inside out. The effort, internally known as Dillas 2.0, would eventually touch nearly every part of the operation, including menu complexity, food preparation, labor deployment, technology, and the brand’s identity. The results have been significant. Dillas has reduced drive-thru service times, improved labor efficiency, stabilized food costs, and returned to positive same-store sales and traffic growth. With 11 restaurants in its system, the company is preparing to resume expansion with a more disciplined strategy and a renewed focus on franchise development. Gordon says the original opening exposed weaknesses that had been manageable when Dillas was smaller but would become difficult to overcome as the brand grew. Kyle Gordon and his wife, Maggie, founded Dillas Quesadillas in 2013. The restaurant’s employees were dealing with complicated preparation procedures, inconsistent production forecasts, and a menu that required customers to navigate numerous combinations. Even with a relatively focused product category, the operation had become unnecessarily difficult to execute. At the time, Dillas offered 10 quesadillas and five side options through a customizable combo system. Customers had to select their quesadilla, decide whether to add a combo, and then choose among the available sides. The variety created opportunities for order inaccuracies and extended the time employees needed to become proficient. The company also relied on experienced employees to estimate how much food needed to be prepared each day. Those estimates weren’t always sufficient during periods of unusually strong demand. Gordon recognized that the system had reached its practical limits. “We basically decided we’re going to keep that quality, but we’re going to lean 100 percent into QSR plus, which is great quality, but you can you can lean on us for convenience, and you can trust us for a level of speed that you just can’t get at a fast casual,” he says. That decision represented a significant change in how Dillas viewed itself. For one day only, Uncle Julio’s will turn back the clock with nostalgic 1986 prices on its signature fajitas, introduce a specially crafted new top-shelf Ruby-flavored margarita, and offer commemorative branded giveaways celebrating the restaurant’s four decades of service. “The first Uncle Julio’s was opened in Dallas with a simple commitment to fresh ingredients and handcrafted recipes, and we have never swayed from that mission. Uncle Julio’s continues to serve made-from scratch Mexican cuisine, using only fresh ingredients and authentic recipes,” says Uncle Julio’s Culinary Artisan of 35-years Rafael Romero. “Today we have 31 stores across 11 states and look forward to serving our legacy customers and welcoming new guests for the next 40 years!” Renowned for its memorable dining experiences and interactive menu, Uncle Julio’s has been creating signature favorites since its inception. In 1986, its iconic lime-and-sangria Swirl Margarita was introduced, and the beloved, exclusive Chocolate Piñata, a made-by-hand chocolate globe filled with homemade mini churros, fresh pineapple and strawberries, was first served nearly a decade ago. Uncle Julio’s will celebrate its 40th anniversary with a one-day celebration on Tuesday, November 17, from 11:00 a.m. to 9 p.m. at all locations. Guests can join the festivities with an exclusive menu created especially for this milestone occasion: – Signature Fajitas – a variety of the mouthwatering staple will return to their original 40-year-ago prices starting at $8.14. – Ruby Margarita – a new signature anniversary hibiscus cinnamon margarita featuring premium 1800 Tequila and Grand Marnier. Balanced with a hint of agave and finished with Fee Foam. – Commemorative Giveaways – The first 40 guests at each restaurant ordering from the Limited Edition 40thAnniversary Menu will receive a commemorative Uncle Julio’s T-shirt. “For 40-years, Uncle Julios has been part of the communities in which it serves. This anniversary celebrates the people, the food and memories that made those 40-years possible. We are grateful beyond words,” concluded Romero. articles.originalSummary: Tommaso Grollero from Italy has been crowned World Chocolate Master 2026, earning one of the most renowned titles in international chocolate craft. The winner was announced on 27 October at Antwerp’s historic Handelsbeurs, following two days of competition among 15 regional champions at the World Chocolate Masters Grand Final. Organised by Callebaut, the World Chocolate Masters brings together leading chocolatiers from around the world to celebrate and advance the craft of chocolate. The finalists competed under the theme “Play & Taste”, taking on four challenges designed to test flavour, technique, artistry, storytelling and commercial thinking. Across the competition, the jury assessed their work for sensory excellence, technical execution, creativity and emotional expression, with taste as the ultimate measure of mastery. “I can’t believe it. Just being among the finalists was already such a great achievement. Over the past nine months, I have worked towards this moment together with my team, and I am deeply grateful to every one of them who helped make it possible. It has been an incredible journey – and winning makes it all the more special,” said Tommaso Grollero. Grollero’s creation, The Invisible , helped set him apart in a field of leading international talent. The work asks a simple question: how do you give shape to something you cannot see? Through an optical illusion, it explores the subjective nature of taste. From one viewpoint, the sculpture presents a familiar, harmonious image; shift perspective, and it transforms into an explosion of shapes and movement, revealing the complexity behind every flavour. “Across the four challenges, Tommaso Grollero showed an exceptional ability to connect flavour, technical precision and a distinctive creative vision. The title is not decided by one striking creation alone; it recognises the consistency and clarity of a chef’s approach to taste. That combination made Tommaso stand out in an exceptionally strong final,” said Amaury Guichon, Head of the World Chocolate Masters jury. Lyu Haoran of China and Keita Koshimizu of Japan completed the podium at the Antwerp Grand Final, taking silver and bronze respectively. Haoran also impressed the jury, winning the Best Bonbon and Best Share awards. Canadian superfinalist Jérémy Monsel received the Best You award, while Grollero added Best Taste and Best Design to his World Chocolate Master title. Sanghwa Lee received the jury standout award. Ian Mark, a chef with 18 years of experience competing on culinary teams, represented the UK and Ireland at this year’s global final. His previous achievements include winning numerous gold medals and accolades for Bake Off: Crème de la Crème , as well as creating the official RAF centenary cake. “The experience has been amazing. I gave it my all and couldn’t have done any more. Nothing fell over, and everything went out on time,” said Ian Mark. “I couldn’t be prouder of what I achieved. It’s been a brilliant experience.” The World Chocolate Master title recognises outstanding creativity, craft and innovation, and has served as a springboard for previous winners’ professional careers. Alongside the distinction itself, the competition offers international visibility and access to a global network of chefs and chocolate professionals. For Grollero, the title marks a major personal achievement and the beginning of new possibilities. Since its first edition in 2005, the World Chocolate Masters has grown into a global celebration of chocolate. By bringing together talented artisans and showcasing their work, it celebrates the diversity of contemporary chocolate craft and offers a glimpse of ideas that may influence the profession in the years to come.
koreanSummary: Tommaso Grollero from Italy has been crowned World Chocolate Master 2026, earning one of the most renowned titles in international chocolate craft.
The winner was announced on 27 October at Antwerp’s historic Handelsbeurs, following two days of competition among 15 regional champions at the World Chocolate Masters Grand Final.
Organised by Callebaut, the World Chocolate Masters brings together leading chocolatiers from around the world to celebrate and advance the craft of chocolate.

articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . Chicken and pork are gaining attention as substitutes, along with seafood options that have become more economically attractive. The next wave of menu innovation may have less to do with discovering the next breakout ingredient and more to do with finding new ways to use what is already in the kitchen. With beef prices putting pressure on food costs, labor challenges complicating operations, and consumers seeking greater variety, restaurants are rethinking everything from protein portions to seasonings. Familiar ingredients are finding new applications, less expensive cuts of meat are gaining attention, and global flavors are giving operators opportunities to introduce new dishes without significantly expanding inventory. Two Sysco culinary experts, Anil Chacko, manager of business specialists in Houston, and Brian Fugit, manager of business specialists for Metro New York, say these developments are influencing menu decisions across the country. Their observations offer a glimpse into how restaurants are adapting to changing consumer expectations and economic conditions as they prepare for 2027. The Protein Equation One of the most immediate challenges is the cost of beef, which continues to influence purchasing decisions and menu development. Restaurants aren’t necessarily eliminating steaks, burgers, and other beef dishes, but they’re becoming more selective with portions, exploring alternative proteins, and finding creative ways to deliver value. Chicken and pork are gaining attention as substitutes, along with seafood options that have become more economically attractive. Shrimp and tuna, in particular, offer an opportunity to introduce ingredients consumers associate with premium dining at price points that are more accessible than in previous years. “Mushrooms have come right back up to the forefront,” Fugit says. “You’re seeing more shredded options with that. King oysters, upcycled shiitakes, and things along that as protein options.” Chacko says operators in South Texas are looking at the same challenges, with chicken, pork, and seafood becoming attractive additions. Beef continues to command strong consumer demand in the region, however, meaning restaurants must find ways to preserve popular menu items without allowing ingredient costs to overwhelm profitability. That has created opportunities for cuts that previously received less attention. Flat iron steaks, for example, can deliver a compelling beef experience without the expense associated with ribeyes, filets, and New York strips. Cooking techniques are helping restaurants make those substitutions more appealing. Fugit notes velveting, a technique associated with Chinese cooking that can improve the tenderness of less expensive cuts of meat. Seasonings are another relatively inexpensive way to create variety. Instead of introducing entirely new proteins or building dishes around costly specialty ingredients, operators can use spice mixtures, dry rubs, and sauces to create different flavor experiences with existing inventory. “People want to see the the maple bourbon dry rubs,” Fugit says. “It’s also a very quick and easy way to change the entire dish and then pivot from that. So if you’re working with neutral proteins carrying three or four dry spices, it’s a great way to target a few different audiences without needing a tremendous amount of skill involved.” Hot honey shows how a relatively simple condiment can create excitement around familiar foods. Its continued popularity has encouraged restaurants to experiment with additional flavor combinations that can be incorporated into existing dishes. articles.title: O consumidor não ficou mais pobre. Ficou mais seletivo
articles.titleKo: O consumidor não ficou mais pobre. Ficou mais seletivo
articles.originalSummary: Existe uma contradição interessante no consumo brasileiro. De um lado, os indicadores mostram um mercado de trabalho relativamente aquecido, aumento da renda e uma massa salarial que continua crescendo. De outro, famílias pressionadas, endividadas e cada vez mais cuidadosas na hora de abrir a carteira. Segundo dados do IBGE , a massa de rendimento real habitual dos brasileiros chegou a R$ 387,5 bilhões em setembro de 2026, crescimento de 4,7% em relação ao mesmo período do ano anterior. É dinheiro novo entrando na economia. Mas, curiosamente, isso não significa que o consumidor esteja necessariamente mais disposto a gastar. O Banco Central ajuda a explicar essa aparente contradição. Em agosto, o endividamento das famílias alcançou 50,1%, enquanto o comprometimento da renda com o pagamento de dívidas chegou a 29%. A Selic permanece em 13,75% ao ano , e a inflação acumulada em 12 meses até setembro estava em 4,58%. Ou seja, parte importante da renda adicional já tem destino antes mesmo de chegar ao desejo de consumo. Mas talvez a questão mais interessante não esteja nos números, e sim no comportamento. O consumidor brasileiro não deixou de desejar. Continua querendo viajar, trocar de celular, frequentar restaurantes, renovar o guarda-roupa e experimentar coisas novas. O que mudou foi a maneira como distribui suas prioridades. Ele pode economizar na compra do supermercado, pesquisar preços em três aplicativos, trocar de marca e aproveitar uma promoção. Mas não necessariamente abrirá mão daquela viagem planejada há meses. Pode escolher uma roupa mais barata e continuar disposto a pagar caro por um bom restaurante ou por uma experiência que considere especial. Parece contraditório? Não é. É o mesmo consumidor fazendo escolhas diferentes, de acordo com o valor que atribui a cada experiência. Durante muito tempo, o varejo se acostumou a segmentar consumidores por renda, idade, classe social e localização. Essas informações continuam importantes, naturalmente. Mas talvez já não sejam suficientes para explicar o comportamento de compra. Duas pessoas com a mesma renda podem ter prioridades completamente diferentes. E uma mesma pessoa pode ser extremamente sensível a preço em uma categoria e pouco sensível em outra. Isso muda bastante a conversa sobre estratégia. O desafio das empresas não é simplesmente descobrir onde estão os consumidores com maior poder aquisitivo, mas entender onde eles estão dispostos a gastar. É uma diferença enorme. Para a indústria, significa rever propostas de valor, embalagens, marcas e arquitetura de preços. Para o varejo, significa ir além da promoção como principal instrumento de conversão. Significa conhecer melhor as missões de compra, entender as categorias que geram valor e identificar onde o cliente aceita pagar mais e onde não aceita pagar nada além do necessário. Existe também uma armadilha nessa discussão: acreditar que o consumidor mais seletivo é necessariamente um consumidor que procura apenas o menor preço. Não é. Ele procura a melhor relação entre aquilo que entrega e aquilo que recebe. E essa percepção muda de acordo com a ocasião, a necessidade e o momento de vida. O varejo que entender isso terá uma vantagem importante. Já aquele que continuar olhando apenas para renda, fluxo de pessoas e volume de vendas poderá descobrir tarde demais que está atraindo consumidores, mas não necessariamente conquistando sua preferência. No final, talvez a grande mudança não seja o consumidor ter menos dinheiro ou mais dinheiro. É que ele está atribuindo um significado diferente a cada real que gasta. E uma pergunta deveria estar presente nas reuniões de planejamento das empresas: estamos realmente entendendo o que faz nosso consumidor escolher onde gastar seu dinheiro ou continuamos tentando vender aquilo que sempre vendemos, esperando que ele continue comprando como sempre comprou? articles.title: Anthropic mira avaliação superior a US$ 1 trilhão em IPO
articles.titleKo: Anthropic mira avaliação superior a US$ 1 trilhão em IPO
articles.originalSummary: A Anthropic, desenvolvedora do assistente de inteligência artificial (IA) Claude, pretende ofertar 825 milhões de ações em sua abertura de capital (IPO), por US$ 70 a US$ 78 cada, segundo prospecto atualizado apresentado nesta terça-feira, 10, à Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC, a CVM dos EUA). A operação poderá movimentar entre US$ 57,75 bilhões e US$ 64,35 bilhões. Do total, 801,35 milhões de ações serão vendidas pela empresa e 23,65 milhões, por acionistas atuais. A Anthropic não receberá recursos da parcela vendida pelos acionistas. A companhia solicitou listagem na Nasdaq, sob o código ANT. O prospecto também prevê uma opção para os bancos coordenadores adquirirem até 123,75 milhões de ações adicionais, o equivalente a 15% da oferta inicial, conforme a demanda. Caso a opção seja integralmente exercida, a operação poderá alcançar 948,75 milhões de papéis e movimentar até US$ 74 bilhões, considerando o teto da faixa indicativa de preços. Após o IPO e a colocação privada, a Anthropic prevê um total de 13,09 bilhões de ações de diferentes classes. No teto da faixa proposta, esse número implica avaliação de cerca de US$ 1,02 trilhão, embora inclua papéis detidos por uma subsidiária integral, não considerados em circulação para fins contábeis. Paralelamente, Google e Nvidia se comprometeram a comprar US$ 10 bilhões em ações cada uma em colocação privada condicionada à conclusão do IPO. A AMD investirá US$ 2,5 bilhões. Broadcom, Micron e Microsoft investirão US$ 1 bilhão cada. A TSMC, US$ 500 milhões. O aporte conjunto soma US$ 26 bilhões e será realização em ações da classe N, sem direito a voto. Parte do compromisso do Google já havia sido assumida anteriormente. Com o preço de US$ 74 por ação, ponto médio da faixa, a Anthropic estima captar US$ 84,6 bilhões líquidos no IPO e na colocação privada, após despesas e comissões. Os recursos serão destinados a operações, pessoal e investimentos em capacidade computacional e infraestrutura. O prospecto lembra que a receita alcançou US$ 17 bilhões no terceiro trimestre de 2026, alta de 1.127% na comparação anual. Nos nove meses até setembro, o faturamento somou US$ 33,24 bilhões, enquanto o prejuízo operacional foi de US$ 1,26 bilhão. Estadão Conteúdo/Pedro Lima Imagem: Divulgação O post Anthropic mira avaliação superior a US$ 1 trilhão em IPO apareceu primeiro em Mercado&Consumo .

articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . KFC is giving its most loyal fans more to love this November with Finger Lickin’ Fan Fest, a limited-time celebration packed with even more ways for KFC Rewards members to get rewarded. From November 11 through November 30, KFC Rewards members can earn 2X points on purchases made through the KFC app or KFC.com, helping fans rack up points toward free food twice as fast. And when it’s time to cash them in, there’s a lot more to choose from: KFC is more than doubling the number of items available in its Secret Recipe Vault, where Rewards members can redeem points for free KFC, expanding from about a dozen choices to 24 different menu items and combos across its 250, 500, 750 and 1,000-point tiers. The timing comes as consumers head into an expensive holiday season with affordability top of mind. The latest Consumer Price Index showed prices up 3.7% year over year in September, while Deloitte found that 38% of shoppers qualify as “holiday value seekers.” With people turning to “ moneymaxxing ” tactics, including loyalty programs, to make the most of their spending, Finger Lickin’ Fan Fest comes at the perfect time before the holidays. Between football watch parties, Friendsgiving, holiday travel and family gatherings, fans have plenty of reasons to order throughout November to get more value every time they choose KFC. “Our KFC Rewards members are some of our biggest fans, and Finger Lickin’ Fan Fest is all about giving them even more back,” said Melissa Cash, Chief Marketing Officer, KFC U.S. “With double points and an expanded Secret Recipe Vault, we’re giving fans more ways to get rewarded for the food they already love.” With an expanded Secret Recipe Vault across four different tiers, members have more flexibility to use their points on what they’re craving, whether they want a quick snack, a side to round out their order or a full meal. New additions include: 250 points: Biscuit 500 points: Large Side, Pot Pie, 2 Pieces of Chicken and 3 Tenders 750 points: Classic Chicken Sandwich Combo, 6 Wings, 3-Piece Tender Combo and 2-Piece Chicken Combo 1,000 points: Big Box 3-Piece Chicken, Big Box 5-Piece Tender and 4-Piece Combo Not a member yet? Fans can sign up for free** to start earning points toward free KFC – plus unlock year-round perks like a welcome offer of 50% off their first purchase, birthday gift and access to exclusive deals. Torali Italian-Steak, the signature restaurant on the 12th floor of The Ritz-Carlton, Chicago, has unveiled its fall and winter menus under Executive Chef Damion Henry, bringing a seasonal perspective to the restaurant’s signature blend of contemporary steakhouse dining and coastal Italian influences. Spanning breakfast, lunch, dinner and cocktails, the refreshed menus showcase seasonal produce, ingredients from regional producers and Italian-inspired preparations suited to Chicago’s colder months. Among the highlights are slow-braised meats, dry-aged specialties designed for sharing and a beverage program featuring cocktails named for the city’s iconic streets and neighborhoods. “I love working with fall and winter ingredients, whether it’s mushrooms, squash or a beautiful cut of meat that benefits from slow cooking,” said Henry. “There’s something special about taking those familiar, comforting flavors and giving them a fresh perspective. Other options include the Westholme Wagyu Steak Frites ($59), featuring a 10-ounce picanha with mushroom ragout, piquillo aioli and french fries, and the Mushroom Ragu ($26) with hand-rolled pasta, basil and breadcrumbs. The 14-Day Dry-Aged Roasted Rohan Duck ($152) is prepared with Torali’s signature spice blend and honey, accompanied by cherry compote, duck confit risotto and natural duck jus, while the 32-ounce Beef Tomahawk Steak ($250) is served with bordelaise, salsa verde, sea salt and olio verde. Alamo Prime Steakhouse, a new Texas steakhouse blending exceptional cuts of beef, Mexican-influenced flavors and genuine hospitality, will officially open its doors on Thursday, November 12, at Grandscape in The Colony. Led by Managing Partner and Executive Chef Jacob Williamson, the new concept from Identity Hospitality Group, a hospitality group led by Managing Partner and industry veteran Marlon Tapanes, brings a fresh perspective to the traditional steakhouse, combining thoughtfully sourced ingredients, a robust beverage program and a warm, inviting atmosphere designed for everything from celebratory dinners and date nights to family gatherings and casual evenings out. Located at 5765 Grandscape Blvd., the 5,200-square-foot restaurant will accommodate approximately 170 guests, including bar seating. Inspired by the rich culture, history and hospitality of Texas, with a particular nod to San Antonio’s heritage, Alamo Prime is built around the belief that the best experiences happen around a full table. At the heart of Alamo Prime is a commitment to genuine hospitality, with an emphasis on creating an experience that feels both elevated and welcoming. Rather than reserving the steakhouse experience for special occasions, Alamo Prime aims to become a place guests return to regularly, whether gathering around the table with family, entertaining clients or enjoying cocktails and dinner at the bar. “Having lived in San Antonio, I developed a real appreciation for the city’s rich history, culture and the way hospitality is so deeply woven into everyday life,” said Marlon Tapanes, Managing Partner of Identity Hospitality Group. “There’s something special about the way people gather around a table there. It’s about more than just the food. It’s about the people you’re sharing it with and the memories you create together. With Alamo Prime, we wanted to bring a piece of that spirit to DFW. Our vision is a place where the table is always full—full of great food, drinks, friends, family and conversation—and where everyone feels welcome.” A defining part of Alamo Prime’s identity is its commitment to Texas agriculture and building lasting relationships with local farmers, ranchers and purveyors. Approximately 50 percent of the restaurant’s Prime beef is sourced from Texas farms and ranches, reflecting the restaurant’s dedication to supporting producers across the state and showcasing the quality and diversity of Texas ingredients. At the helm of the kitchen is Managing Partner and Executive Chef Jacob Williamson, a Dallas native and fourth-generation Texan with more than 15 years of culinary experience. Throughout his career, Williamson has built lasting relationships with Texas farmers, ranchers and local purveyors, making locally sourced, seasonal ingredients a signature of his culinary approach. His longstanding commitment to supporting Texas producers aligns with Alamo Prime’s own philosophy of prioritizing local sourcing and building meaningful relationships with the people behind its ingredients. “We wanted to create a steakhouse that celebrates the quality of Texas ingredients while feeling like a place people can enjoy any night of the week,” said Williamson. “Of course, the steaks are a major part of what we do, but there’s so much more to the experience. From the relationships we’ve built with local ranchers and farmers to the flavors we’re bringing to the menu, every detail has been thoughtfully considered. Our goal is to serve exceptional food while making every guest feel genuinely welcome.” The culinary program celebrates Texas ingredients and ranching traditions with Mexican influences woven throughout the menu. articles.title: Southerleigh Hospitality Group to Open Haute South in San Antonio’s River North District
articles.titleKo: Southerleigh Hospitality Group to Open Haute South in San Antonio’s River North District
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . Southerleigh Hospitality Group is bringing Haute South to River North in San Antonio, announcing the relocation of its popular Southern-inspired concept from The RIM to Make Ready Market, located at 203 8th Street. Slated to open in early December 2026, the move marks a new chapter for Haute South and another milestone in the group’s strategic growth, expanding its portfolio into the fast-casual dining space with a concept rooted in the bold flavors of the Texas Gulf Coast. The relocation follows the group’s expansion of Southerleigh at San Antonio International Airport (SAT) earlier this year, reflecting its vision to bring its distinctive culinary concepts to new audiences and dining environments beyond traditional full-service restaurants. Together, these developments signal the group’s continued evolution and commitment to growing its presence across San Antonio and beyond. Having built a loyal following at The RIM, Haute South will retain its signature approach to Southern cooking while embracing a more approachable, fast-casual format. Its new home at Make Ready Market, a locally curated food hall in San Antonio’s vibrant River North District, places the concept among an eclectic mix of independently owned culinary destinations. Known for bringing diverse food experiences together under one roof, Make Ready Market offers an ideal setting for Haute South to showcase its signature Southern comfort food and Texas Gulf Coast-inspired flavors to a new audience of locals and visitors. Menu highlights include: Texas Raw Oysters: Served with classic cocktail sauce, BBQ mignonette, fresh horseradish and lemon. Caviar Service: An elevated indulgence for guests looking to start with something special. Pimento Queso: Southern-inspired queso blended with pimento, with pickled jalapeños served on the side. Famous Fried Chicken: Texas-raised chicken, pressure-fried to golden perfection and served with a fried biscuit and signature Haute Sauce. Southern Fried Chicken Sandwich: A crispy fried chicken breast served as a Southern comfort-food favorite. Texas Gulf Shrimp Basket: Half a pound of Gulf shrimp, lightly breaded or blackened, accompanied by comeback and rémoulade sauces. Guests can also enjoy Haute South’s daily Happy Hour from 4–7 p.m., featuring select specials including $1.50 single oysters, $3 Southerleigh Gold Lager, $4 El Perrito Margaritas and $9 Tsar Nicoulai caviar bumps. “We’re incredibly proud of everything Haute South has built at The RIM, and we’re excited about what this next chapter represents,” said Jeff Balfour, Co-founder of Southerleigh Hospitality Group. “Make Ready is a destination that attracts curious, food-loving guests who appreciate quality, creativity and a great dining experience. This move gives us an opportunity to bring the best of Haute South to a more approachable, fast-casual setting while staying true to our Texas Gulf Coast roots. It’s also an important step in our vision for growing the concept and expanding our presence in the fast-casual dining landscape.” Haute South’s current location at The RIM will close November 15, 2026, with the team preparing for its debut at Make Ready Market in early December. Guests can follow Haute South and Southerleigh Hospitality Group on social media for opening updates and additional announcements. “Haute South captures what we love about San Antonio’s food scene: local roots, great food, and a loyal following. Their full bar is a welcome addition to Make Ready, and we’re excited to have them in River North,” said Jenine Cournoyer, General Manager, Make Ready Market. COJE Management Group, the hospitality company behind some of Boston’s most celebrated restaurants and nightlife destinations, has named Colin Lynch executive chef of two forthcoming concepts at 10 Post Office Square. The appointment comes as COJE prepares for a major expansion at the downtown Boston address, tripling its existing footprint. The new space will introduce a two-level Nomadic Italian restaurant and, beneath it, a private members club where the kitchen takes its cues from itameshi, the Japanese reinterpretation of Italian cuisine. He began his career at Barbara Lynch Gruppo, where he rose from chef de cuisine at No. 9 Park to executive chef of the restaurant group, helping develop award-winning concepts including Menton and Sportello. He went on to lead the kitchen at the critically acclaimed Japanese restaurant o ya, a stretch that shaped the Italian-meets-Japanese sensibility he later brought to his own restaurants, including Bar Mezzana, Shore Leave and No Relation. articles.title: Ata do Copom indica que desaceleração da economia não conteve inflação
articles.titleKo: Ata do Copom indica que desaceleração da economia não conteve inflação
articles.originalSummary: A ata do Comitê de Política Monetária (Copom) divulgada nesta terça-feira, 10, indica que a atividade econômica brasileira dá sinais mais claros de desaceleração, enquanto a inflação continua pressionada. Nesse cenário, o Banco Central reforçou a avaliação de que a Selic deverá permanecer em nível restritivo por mais tempo. Segundo o documento, os indicadores mais recentes apontam para uma “moderação mais acentuada da atividade econômica, principalmente em setores mais cíclicos”. Apesar da perda de fôlego da demanda, a inflação voltou a acelerar e permanece acima do limite de tolerância da meta definida pelo Conselho Monetário Nacional (CMN). Mercado de trabalho A ata também destaca o comportamento do mercado de trabalho. Embora a taxa de desemprego permaneça em níveis historicamente baixos, o crescimento da ocupação perdeu força. “A taxa de desemprego mantém-se em patamares historicamente baixos, enquanto o crescimento da taxa de ocupação vem apresentando desaceleração.” Os rendimentos médios perderam força na margem, mas continuam crescendo acima da produtividade do trabalho. O Copom observa que eles “ainda crescem em termos reais a uma taxa superior à da produtividade do trabalho”, aspecto monitorado pelo BC por seus possíveis reflexos sobre a inflação. Outro ponto de preocupação é a piora das expectativas de inflação. As projeções do mercado para os próximos anos continuaram se afastando da meta de 3%. Na avaliação do comitê, “em um ambiente de expectativas desancoradas, como é o caso do atual, exige-se uma restrição monetária maior e por mais tempo do que outrora seria apropriado”. A ata também voltou a destacar a importância da política fiscal para o controle da inflação. Segundo o documento, incertezas sobre a estabilização da dívida pública e um eventual esmorecimento do esforço de reformas estruturais e disciplina fiscal podem dificultar a convergência da inflação para a meta. O Copom reiterou ainda a “necessidade de políticas fiscal e monetária harmoniosas”. Cenário externo Além dos fatores domésticos, o Banco Central avalia que o cenário internacional se tornou mais adverso desde a reunião anterior. A ata atribui essa mudança ao prolongamento dos conflitos no Oriente Médio , que elevou os preços do petróleo, e à manutenção de condições monetárias restritivas nas economias avançadas. Segundo o documento, esse ambiente exige cautela dos países emergentes em um contexto marcado por “elevação da volatilidade de preços de ativos e commodities ”. Choques de oferta O Copom afirma que o cenário atual combina sinais mais claros de desaceleração da economia doméstica com quatro choques de oferta: a alta do petróleo provocada pelos conflitos no Oriente Médio; os efeitos do El Niño sobre a produção agrícola e os custos de energia; os impactos do fim da escala 6×1 sobre os custos do trabalho; e a desvalorização do real frente ao dólar. O Copom avalia que esses fatores continuam pressionando o cenário inflacionário. Ao mesmo tempo, considera que a desaceleração mais intensa da atividade econômica pode reduzir o risco de que esses choques se espalhem para outros setores da economia e gerem pressões inflacionárias mais persistentes. articles.title: Cartões movimentam R$ 1,2 tri no 3º trimestre; crescimento é de 6,6% em um ano
articles.titleKo: Cartões movimentam R$ 1,2 tri no 3º trimestre; crescimento é de 6,6% em um ano
articles.originalSummary: O setor de cartões movimentou R$ 1,2 trilhão em volume transacionado (TPV, na sigla em inglês) no terceiro trimestre de 2026, de acordo com a Associação Brasileira das Empresas de Cartões de Crédito e Serviços ( Abecs ), em coletiva de imprensa. O resultado representa um crescimento de 6,6% em relação a igual período de 2025. O número representa um desaceleração , considerando que no segundo trimestre a expansão havia sido de 7,7% e no primeiro de 8,3%. Os cartões de crédito movimentaram R$ 874,2 bilhões, uma alta de 10% em 12 meses. Já os cartões de débito recuaram 1% no período, a R$ 245,4 bilhões, enquanto o cartão pré-pago registrou recuo de 2,2%, a R$ 96,6 bilhões. O presidente da Abecs, Giancarlo Greco, classificou os números como robustos, sobretudo no crédito, apesar do trimestre desafiador para a economia. Segundo ele, o cenário atual favorece produtos com limite de crédito, o que ajuda a explicar o avanço dessa modalidade e a queda do débito. No terceiro trimestre, os brasileiros efetuaram 12,4 bilhões de transações com cartões, uma alta de 2,3% no confronto anual. Isso significa que foram feitos 135 milhões de pagamentos por dia, em média. Do total de transações no trimestre, 5,8 bilhões de operações foram com cartões de crédito, alta de 6,2%. No débito, foram 4,2 bilhões de operações, alta de 0,4%. Projeções A Abecs reduziu a previsão do crescimento do volume transacionado com cartões em 2026, para o intervalo de 7,5% a 9,5%. A previsão anterior era de expansão entre 9,5% a 11,5% este ano. Com essa nova previsão, esses meios de pagamento podem movimentar entre R$ 4,88 trilhões a R$ 4,97 trilhões em 2026. Em 2025, os cartões cresceram 10,1%, com TPV de R$ 4,55 trilhões. Greco ressaltou que o ano começou forte para o setor, mas perdeu ritmo no segundo trimestre e voltou a mostrar desaceleração no período mais recente. Entre os fatores, citou o menor crescimento do comércio e o endividamento das famílias . “Isso fez com que revisássemos a projeção, muito em função do comportamento da economia”, disse em entrevista coletiva. Com informação do Estadão de Conteúdo (Altamiro Silva Junior). articles.title: Starbucks acelera expansão e amplia presença no Nordeste com estreia no Ceará
articles.titleKo: Starbucks acelera expansão e amplia presença no Nordeste com estreia no Ceará
articles.originalSummary: A Starbucks, operada no Brasil pela Zamp , prepara uma nova rodada de expansão e vai chegar ao Ceará. Até o fim de 2026, a rede planeja inaugurar cerca de 10 unidades em São Paulo, Belo Horizonte e Fortaleza. A capital cearense marca a estreia da marca no estado e reforça sua presença no Nordeste. Por lá, estão previstas duas lojas no Fortaleza Airport e uma no Shopping Iguatemi Bosque. A expansão traz ainda novos formatos de loja. Em 2027, a Starbucks pretende abrir duas unidades no Beto Carrero World, uma delas na área temática Cowboyland. “Nossa conexão com o Brasil é de longa data. Junto com a Zamp, estamos fortalecendo essa base por meio de um crescimento planejado e com propósito, focado em oferecer as experiências certas, nos lugares certos”, afirma Ricardo Arias-Nath, vice-presidente sênior global de Café e Chá e presidente da Starbucks para América Latina e Caribe. À medida que amplia sua presença no Brasil, a rede também tem incluído produtos inspirados nos hábitos de consumo dos brasileiros em seu cardápio. Um exemplo é o Cafezinho Brasileiro, lançado com referência à tradição nacional de consumo da bebida. O cardápio também inclui produtos conhecidos, como pão de queijo, Brigadeiro e Frappuccino, além de bebidas desenvolvidas localmente, como o Média Pingado. Para o fim do ano, a Starbucks prepara o lançamento de bebidas especiais de Natal e o retorno do Panettone ao cardápio, com produtos disponíveis nas lojas de todo o País. Marca abre três lojas no Rio de Janeiro A Starbucks retomou a expansão no Rio de Janeiro com a abertura de três lojas na cidade. A primeira foi inaugurada no Shopping Tijuca, seguida por unidades no Aeroporto Internacional Tom Jobim (Galeão) e no Shopping Rio Sul, em Botafogo. A abertura das unidades marca o retorno da rede a regiões do Rio de Janeiro onde já esteve presente e integra o plano de expansão no País. A empresa prevê cerca de 30 novas lojas no Brasil até o fim de 2026. As lojas seguem o conceito global Community Coffee House , com diferentes configurações de assentos e espaços destinados a encontros, trabalho e permanência dos clientes. articles.titleKo: Nick the Greek Opens in Indio, California
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Nick the Greek, a national chain serving authentic Greek street food, is now open in Indio, marking its debut in the Coachella Valley. The new location is locally owned and operated by husband-and-wife Freeman and Kelly Swank and their son Tony. For more than a decade, Nick the Greek has proved that “The Best Things in Life are Greek” through a diverse and enticing menu of tasty pitas, bowls, salads, desserts and more — now available to Indio locals and visitors at the brand’s newest Nick the Greek location. “We decided to open a Nick the Greek in Indio to meet local demand for Greek food and, after experiencing Nick the Greek’s food and hospitality ourselves, we knew this is what we wanted to introduce to our community,” said Freeman Swank. “As local residents for 15 years, we are proud to bring an authentic Greek street food experience to our neighbors and seasonal festival goers while looking forward to expanding with additional Nick the Greek restaurants throughout the Coachella Valley.” Established in 2014 by cousins Big Nick, Little Nick and Baby Nick Tsigaris — all named after their grandfather per Greek tradition — Nick the Greek satisfies the desire for healthy, flavorful and authentic Greek cuisine in a fast casual environment without compromising quality. Today, guests can find Nick the Greek restaurants in eight states, including Arizona, California, Kansas, Missouri, Nevada, Tennessee, Texas and Utah. articles.title: Grupo brasileiro compra dona das marcas Maguary e Dafruta por 80 milhões de euros
articles.titleKo: Grupo brasileiro compra dona das marcas Maguary e Dafruta por 80 milhões de euros
articles.originalSummary: O Carlsberg Group anunciou que assinou acordo para vender a Empresa Brasileira de Bebidas e Alimentos SA (Britvic Brazil), fabricante de sucos como Maguary e Dafruta, ao Grupo José Augusto Vieira (Grupo JAV) pelo valor de 80 milhões de euros. Segundo comunicado, a conclusão da transação é esperada até dezembro de 2026, sujeita a aprovações regulatórias. A Carlsberg informou que decidiu vender a operação brasileira após uma revisão estratégica. A companhia havia assumido o controle da Britvic Brazil em janeiro de 2025, quando adquiriu o negócio internacional de refrigerantes da Britvic plc. Do lado comprador, Frank Vieira, acionista do Grupo JAV, disse que a aquisição é um marco para o grupo e reflete “confiança de longo prazo” no mercado brasileiro. A Carlsberg disse que o BofA Securities atuou como assessor financeiro exclusivo, e o escritório Lefosse como assessor legal. Movimentações de compra agitam o setor de alimentos Outra movimentação envolvendo aquisições no setor de alimentos envolve a JBS . A companhia apresentou uma proposta para comprar os cerca de 18% das ações da Pilgrim’s Pride que ainda não pertencem ao frigorífico brasileiro ou a suas subsidiárias. O Conselho de Administração da norte-americana Pilgrim’s Pride informou, em documento enviado à Comissão de Valores Mobiliários dos Estados Unidos (SEC, na sigla em inglês), que formará um comitê especial de membros independentes para avaliar a proposta não vinculante apresentada pela acionista controladora JBS N.V. Segundo o documento, não há garantia de que a oferta resultará na conclusão da transação. Caso a transação seja validada pelo comitê independente e pela maioria dos votos dos acionistas minoritários não afiliados, as ações da Pilgrim’s deixarão de ser negociadas publicamente e a empresa terá seu registro cancelado na Bolsa de Nova York. *Conteúdo elaborado com auxílio de inteligência artificial, revisado e editado pela Redação do Broadcast, sistema de notícias em tempo real do Grupo Estado Com informação do Estadão de Conteúdo (Luísa Laval). articles.title: Amy D’s Italian to Open in Downtown Frisco Next Year

articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . Amy D’s Italian is set to open Spring 2027 at 7511 Main Street in Downtown Frisco, bringing Chef Amy DiBiase’s Italian heritage and more than two decades of culinary experience to The Patios at the Rail, a catalytic development in the heart of Downtown Frisco. The two-level restaurant from Nack Hospitality will offer an elevated yet approachable Italian dining experience, equally suited for date nights, family dinners and everything in between, featuring handcrafted pasta, wood-grilled specialties and an upstairs Aperitivo Lounge. Raised in Maine, DiBiase learned to cook beside her Italian grandmother and in her family’s restaurants before earning degrees from Johnson & Wales University. She went on to lead the kitchens at Tidal and the InterContinental Hotel in San Diego and most recently served as Executive Chef of Elaine’s Kitchen. “Some of my favorite memories are of making pasta with my grandmother, and that’s the feeling I want every guest to have at Amy D’s,” says DiBiase. “I look forward to bringing that to Frisco, with the best ingredients from Texas and Italy.” Amy D’s is a partnership between DiBiase and Donny Churchman, founder and CEO of Nack Companies and developer of The Patios at the Rail. It arrives as Downtown Frisco gains momentum following the city’s $83 million makeover of The Rail District, and fills a gap downtown for elevated Italian that’s still family-friendly. Amy D’s is the first of several planned Nack Hospitality concepts, with DiBiase leading culinary direction and operations across the group. “When we developed The Patios at the Rail, we wanted to establish a destination that would help redefine Downtown Frisco,” says Churchman. “Amy D’s represents everything we envisioned for The Patios: great food, exceptional hospitality and an atmosphere that gives people another reason to fall in love with Downtown Frisco.” The chef-driven menu pairs ingredients sourced from Texas and Italy with regional Italian inspiration, moving from antipasti and housemade focaccia to handcrafted pastas, wood-grilled specialties and seasonal sides made for sharing. A dedicated pasta room lets guests see the craft behind every plate. The bar pours Italian-focused wines, classic and signature cocktails and spritzes, plus housemade shrubs, Italian sodas and alcohol-free spritzes. Upstairs, the Aperitivo Lounge will host Aperitivo Hour Tuesday through Saturday from 4 to 7 p.m. On Friday and Saturday nights, “Dopo Notte”, late-night service carries the evening forward with cocktails, wine and Italian-inspired bites from 10 p.m. to 1 a.m. Designed by Maybeck Design, the 4,700-square-foot space pairs a warm neighborhood dining room of walnut, creamy stone and aged brass, centered on the bar and working pasta kitchen, with a moodier, speakeasy-inspired second floor in deep olive, bronze and saturated red. The enclosed rooftop space features lush greenery, layered lighting, and bold furnishings, creating a lively yet sophisticated setting for gathering, celebrating and enjoying an evening out. Sliding glass panels can open the space to the outdoors when weather permits, offering a seamless indoor-outdoor experience. A 20-seat private dining room provides an intimate setting for special occasions. “Our vision for Amy D’s was to create a restaurant that feels timeless without feeling traditional,” says Danielle Harbeck, founder and CEO of Maybeck Design. Amy D’s Italian will initially serve dinner Tuesday through Saturday from 4 to 10 p.m., with plans to introduce a special Sunday Italian Lunch at a later date. Inspired by the Sundays Chef Amy spent gathered around her grandmother’s table, the multi-course, family-style experience will celebrate the tradition of sharing good food and making memories with loved ones. Additional menu and opening details will be announced soon. For updates, visit www.amydsitalian.c

articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Same-store sales fell 6.4 percent in Q3, including a 4.9 percent traffic decline. Sweetgreen’s collaboration with Molly Baz gave customers a reason to talk about the brand—and come back for lunch. For CEO Jonathan Neman, it also offered a lesson in how the company should approach its next round of menu launches. The pickle-heavy partnership worked because culinary, marketing, and restaurant operations came together, he said. Sweetgreen wants to carry that coordination into 2027, with six major “experience windows” and smaller drops between them. Planning further ahead gives teams more time to refine recipes, prepare restaurants, and train employees. “The lesson is a little bit fewer, but bigger, better things,” Neman said during Sweetgreen’s third-quarter earnings call. READ MORE : Sweetgreen Introduces Incentive Plan with $200,000-Plus Potential for Restaurant Managers Sweetgreen Finds More Ways to Grow After a Wraps Win, Sweetgreen Faces a Fresh Setback That approach comes as the fast casual begins to regain traffic following a summer setback. Same-store sales fell 6.4 percent in Q3, including a 4.9 percent traffic decline. Sweetgreen estimates the disruption surrounding cyclospora headlines reduced traffic by approximately 500 basis points. By October, comps were up about 5 percent, driven by approximately 4 percent transaction growth. Neman said momentum improved further heading into November. The recovery is coming primarily from existing customers visiting more frequently and lapsed guests returning. New-customer acquisition is improving, Neman said, but remains a smaller contributor. The Baz collaboration brought three limited-time offerings to restaurants, including the Big Dill Caesar Wrap. Neman described it as one of Sweetgreen’s strongest recent brand moments and sees potential to make the Chef in Residence a repeatable platform. “The Molly collaboration really resonated both from a social and brand awareness perspective, but it was also delicious and well executed, and customers really just loved it,” he said. Sweetgreen did not quantify the partnership’s sales contribution. But it reinforced the role wraps are playing in improving frequency and reaching younger diners. Wrap incidence has remained in the high teens, with a recent increase following the collaboration. The Chicken Caesar Wrap now has the menu’s highest return rate, according to Neman. Those lower-priced options carry a trade-off. Wraps help bring customers back but pressure sales mix. Sweetgreen is reducing its reliance on discounts while maintaining everyday entry points alongside premium offerings. The next opportunity sits at dinner, which accounts for only about one-third of sales after 5 p.m. Sweetgreen is preparing to put Plates back in the spotlight with larger rotisserie-style chicken and a freshly baked sourdough chocolate chip cookie. The preparations extend beyond marketing. Sweetgreen has strengthened oven infrastructure, cooking tools, and kitchen-leader training as it expands further into hot food. That work connects to a broader issue the chain has been addressing throughout its turnaround: getting more restaurants to perform like its best ones. Forty locations set peak-hour records during September and October. Yet Neman said the gap between top-performing and median restaurants remains significant. “It is a clear reminder that two restaurants can have the same menu, equipment, and systems and still deliver very different experiences,” he said. “The difference is the head coach.” Sweetgreen’s new head coach incentive plan , taking effect in Q1 2027, ties compensation more closely to restaurant volume, sales growth, and tenure. articles.originalSummary: A Boca Rosa, marca de maquiagem fundada por Bianca Andrade, inaugurou um escritório corporativo em São Paulo para acompanhar o crescimento do negócio, e a nova sede amplia a capacidade de 60 para até 100 colaboradores. “O escritório é símbolo de um momento muito importante pra Boca Rosa. Conforme a empresa vai crescendo e se desenvolvendo, precisamos que a nossa estrutura acompanhe essa evolução. Queremos que as pessoas se sintam parte da construção da marca”, afirma Bianca Andrade, fundadora e CEO da Boca Rosa. A mudança também reorganiza o dia a dia da equipe. Times que antes estavam espalhados por diferentes andares agora dividem o mesmo pavimento, o que deve facilitar a integração entre as áreas e a troca de ideias. O espaço ganhou mais salas de reunião, ambientes para conversas individuais, copa ampliada e melhorias em conectividade e ergonomia. A identidade visual do espaço reúne os tons de rosa da marca e elementos característicos, como a boquinha. O ambiente também inclui áreas voltadas ao conforto dos colaboradores e espaços para eventos internos, encontros e reuniões com parceiros da Boca Rosa. O crescimento da equipe segue no radar da companhia, que avalia continuamente as necessidades da operação e as oportunidades de incorporar novos talentos de forma estratégica e sustentável. articles.title: Gás do Povo libera vale-recarga para 3,1 milhões de famílias
articles.titleKo: Gás do Povo libera vale-recarga para 3,1 milhões de famílias
articles.originalSummary: A Caixa Econômica Federal libera nesta terça-feira, 10, o vale-recarga do programa Gás do Povo para cerca de 3,1 milhões de famílias. A iniciativa do governo federal permite a retirada gratuita de um botijão de gás de cozinha de 13 quilos (GLP) em revendedoras credenciadas. Segundo a Caixa, mais de 15 milhões de famílias foram contempladas pelo programa. Como retirar o botijão Para receber a recarga, o responsável familiar deve procurar uma das 27 mil revendedoras que aderiram ao programa em todo o País. A validação do benefício é feita eletronicamente, na maquininha azulzinha da Caixa, por uma das seguintes opções: Cartão com chip do Bolsa Família : apresentação do cartão e uso da senha; Cartão de débito da Caixa: com senha da conta; CPF: informado na maquininha, com código de validação enviado por SMS ao telefone cadastrado na Caixa. A consulta ao direito ao benefício e à lista de revendedoras participantes pode ser feita pelos seguintes canais: Aplicativo Meu Social – Gás do Povo; Site do Ministério do Desenvolvimento Social; Portal Cidadão Caixa; Atendimento Caixa Cidadão: 111 ou 0800-726-0207; Site da Caixa; Disque Social: 121. Frequência do benefício Os vales são liberados no dia 10 de cada mês. A quantidade de recargas disponíveis ao longo do ano depende do número de integrantes da família registrado no Cadastro Único (CadÚnico). A periodicidade é dividida da seguinte forma: Famílias com dois ou três integrantes: um vale a cada três meses; Famílias com quatro ou mais integrantes: um vale a cada dois meses. Quem tem direito? A seleção dos beneficiários é feita pelo Ministério do Desenvolvimento e Assistência Social, Família e Combate à Fome (MDS). Para ser escolhido, é preciso ter: Inscrição no Cadastro Único; Renda familiar mensal de até meio salário mínimo por pessoa; Cadastro atualizado há pelo menos 24 meses. Famílias que recebem o Bolsa Família têm prioridade no acesso ao programa. Redução da pobreza energética O Gás do Povo é uma política pública federal que substitui o Auxílio Gás dos Brasileiros e busca ampliar o acesso ao gás de cozinha entre famílias de baixa renda. O programa oferece a recarga gratuita de botijões de GLP de 13 quilos em estabelecimentos credenciados e tem previsão de alcançar cerca de 50 milhões de pessoas. Para participar, os estabelecimentos precisam estar cadastrados na Agência Nacional do Petróleo, Gás Natural e Biocombustíveis (ANP), regulares junto à Receita Federal, ter conta corrente de pessoa jurídica na Caixa e utilizar a maquininha azulzinha. A Caixa é responsável pela operacionalização do benefício e pelo sistema de adesão das revendedoras. Dúvidas podem ser esclarecidas pelo Disque Social 121, pelo canal FalaBR ou pelo SAC da Caixa, no telefone 0800 726 0101. O atendimento humano do Disque Social funciona de segunda a sexta-feira, das 7h às 19h. O atendimento eletrônico está disponível 24 horas por dia. Com informações de Agência Brasil Imagem: Marcello Casal/Agência Brasil O post Gás do Povo libera vale-recarga para 3,1 milhões de famílias apareceu primeiro em Mercado&Consumo .

articles.titleKo: Como saúde e longevidade estão transformando a indústria de alimentos
articles.originalSummary: Durante décadas, a indústria de alimentos construiu seu crescimento em torno de sabor, conveniência e indulgência. Esses atributos continuarão sendo determinantes. Porém, uma nova dimensão ganha força: a capacidade dos alimentos de entregar benefícios concretos de saúde, nutrição e qualidade de vida. Essa mudança acompanha uma transformação mais ampla no comportamento do consumidor. Em uma sociedade que envelhece e quer viver mais e melhor, alimentação deixa de ser apenas uma questão de prazer ou praticidade e passa a ser parte ativa da estratégia de saúde e longevidade. Os consumidores estão cada vez mais atentos à composição nutricional dos produtos e aos seus impactos na composição corporal, prevenção, energia e cognição. Nesse contexto, poucos ingredientes representam essa transformação tão claramente quanto o whey protein. Antes restrito ao universo esportivo, o whey começa a ocupar um espaço muito mais amplo na alimentação cotidiana, tornando-se plataforma de inovação para diferentes categorias de alimentos e bebidas. Os números mostram a velocidade dessa mudança. Em estudo inédito no Brasil, a Bain & Company estima que o mercado brasileiro de concentrados e isolados proteicos derivados do leite passou de aproximadamente US$ 170 milhões em 2021 para cerca de US$ 360 milhões em 2025. O crescimento revela também uma sofisticação da categoria: enquanto o WPC-80, principal referência do mercado, cresceu cerca de 9% ao ano em volume, o WPI, segmento de maior concentração proteica, avançou mais de 20% ao ano no período. Ainda assim, o Brasil tem menos da metade do consumo per capita de WPC-80 dos Estados Unidos. Para os próximos cinco anos, a expectativa é de que o crescimento continue, em torno de 7% ao ano em volume. Um dos principais aceleradores dessa transformação será o avanço das terapias emagrecedoras, os GLP-1 . De acordo com a última edição do Consumer Pulse (pesquisa anual da Bain com mais de 2 mil consumidores) , o Brasil já apresenta adoção relevante: cerca de 11% da população já utilizou ou utiliza essas medicações, próximo ao patamar americano de 15%. As projeções indicam que mais de 20% dos brasileiros poderão ter usado essas terapias até 2030. O impacto sobre a alimentação é direto. Ao reduzirem o apetite e promoverem perda de peso, essas terapias colocam uma questão central: como perder gordura preservando massa muscular. Nesse contexto, a proteína deixa de ser um suplemento esportivo e passa a ser uma ferramenta nutricional. Os consumidores que usam GLP-1 apresentam consumo de whey protein quase duas vezes superior ao dos praticantes de atividade física que não utilizam essas terapias. E o efeito não é passageiro: a queda de patentes em 2026 deve baratear o acesso, novas formulações em comprimido devem ampliar a adesão, e o efeito rebote tende a gerar ciclos recorrentes de uso. Além do GLP-1 Mas a transformação não se limita a quem usa GLP-1. Os praticantes de atividade física que não recorrem a essas terapias respondem por 60% da demanda total de whey no Brasil. A busca por longevidade e melhor composição corporal já criou novos hábitos em uma parcela crescente da população. O medicamento apenas acelera uma mudança que já estava em curso. A indústria começa a responder. Empresas de alimentos e bebidas reformulam portfólios e criam produtos que combinam proteína, fibras e outros atributos funcionais para seus consumidores. A próxima geração de produtos deverá ser transparente quanto aos benefícios que entregam, como saciedade, praticidade, suporte à manutenção muscular e adequação a usuários de GLP-1. Esse espaço de inovação também altera a dinâmica competitiva. Marcas insurgentes, construídas em comunidades digitais de saúde e bem-estar, capturaram consumidores ao associar produtos a objetivos claros de performance. articles.title: Yo-Chi confirms second UK site to open in Clapham
articles.titleKo: Yo-Chi confirms second UK site to open in Clapham
articles.originalSummary: Australian frozen yoghurt brand Yo-Chi has announced it will open its second UK venue on Bromell’s Road in Clapham later this year, four months after making its UK debut in Notting Hill. The 1,850 sq ft site will have seating for 60 guests indoors and a further 30 outdoors. It follows the opening of the brand’s first UK venue on Notting Hill Gate in August, which attracted queues of more than five and a half hours on its opening day. Since launching in the UK, Yo-Chi has served more than 100,000 bowls, with its Signature Tart flavour proving the most popular among customers. The Clapham venue will operate the brand’s self-serve, pay-by-weight format, offering ten signature frozen yoghurt flavours and real açaí, alongside a toppings station featuring more than 30 ingredients. These include fresh fruit, choc chunk cookie cake and mini mochi.

articles.title: Outback Steakhouse is Getting Better. Now It Needs More Customers
articles.titleKo: Outback Steakhouse is Getting Better. Now It Needs More Customers
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . Outback Steakhouse's same-store sales rose 1.9 percent in Q3. Outback Steakhouse is giving servers fewer tables and customers another reason to leave their grills untouched. The harder task is getting more people through the door. Bloomin’ Brands’ third-quarter results showed progress inside its largest chain’s restaurants, with guest satisfaction improving for a fifth consecutive quarter. But those gains have not translated into traffic growth. Outback’s same-store sales increased 1.9 percent, supported by higher average checks, as visits declined 1.5 percent. The company is resisting another immediate menu price increase to help close that gap. Bloomin’ delayed planned fourth-quarter pricing at Outback and Bonefish Grill, accepting a smaller near-term sales contribution as it works to make dining out worth the expense. “We just don’t feel we need to take more pricing than inflation. It really boils down to that,” CEO Michael Spanos said during the earnings call. READ MORE : Outback’s Journey to Reignite a ‘Remarkable Dining Experience’ Continues Why Outback is Reducing Table Counts for Servers Outback Steakhouse Sees First Traffic Growth in Years as Turnaround Gains Traction The decision captures the balancing act behind Outback’s turnaround. Bloomin’ is paying for better food, additional service capacity, restaurant refreshes, and more advertising in a business still losing customers. Savings from scheduling, purchasing, and utility controls are helping fund those improvements without pulling resources from the dining experience. Across its U.S. portfolio, comparable sales increased 1.9 percent, with traffic declining 1.8 percent and average check rising 3.7 percent. Sales growth trailed the Black Box Intelligence benchmark by 120 basis points, and traffic lagged by 180 basis points. Total revenue reached $944 million, compared with $929 million a year earlier. Excluding approximately $13 million associated with a gift card accounting estimate change, revenue was essentially flat. The adjusted loss widened to 17 cents per share from 3 cents. Adjusted restaurant-level operating margin declined 20 basis points to 9.3 percent, and adjusted operating margin fell to 0.3 percent from 0.8 percent. Commodity inflation reached 4.6 percent, and labor inflation was 3.5 percent. Outback’s recovery starts with making those restaurant investments visible to guests. Its updated service model limits servers to four tables during peak hours, compared with six historically. Front-of-house hospitality training followed in August. Spanos said the smaller sections reduce the strain created when an unexpected absence leaves a server covering too many tables. Employees are earning the same amount or slightly more under the new model, helped by lower tip-sharing obligations and modestly higher tip percentages. The changes are registering in customer feedback. Outback’s service, atmosphere, and likelihood-to-return scores each improved three points from a year earlier. Value increased two points, and food improved one point. Spanos said the chain’s scores now match or exceed key competitors. Steak preparation is another priority. The steak lineup launched last November continues to earn strong guest ratings, and multiunit operators will complete annual steak certification training again next month before certifying restaurant teams. Outback also finished expanding its chargrill equipment, giving kitchens more cooking capacity across steak and other proteins. That work preceded October’s Best Steaks Ever campaign. Spanos said the company wanted restaurant execution and service in place before making a larger advertising push. Bloomin’ increased annual marketing investment by $10 million, concentrated in the second half. By year-end, its media allocation is expected to reach approximately 60 percent digital and 40 percent tradition

articles.title: Restaurant Technology Should Fit the Manager’s Workflow, Not the Other Way Around
articles.titleKo: Restaurant Technology Should Fit the Manager’s Workflow, Not the Other Way Around
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . The most effective restaurant technology should complement existing operations rather than compete for attention. Restaurant managers operate in an environment where priorities can change by the minute. Between overseeing employees, managing schedules, addressing unexpected staffing issues, and ensuring guests have a positive experience, their attention is constantly being pulled in different directions. Technology is supposed to help simplify these responsibilities, yet too often, it introduces additional steps into an already demanding workday. Over the years, we’ve spent considerable time speaking with restaurant owners, franchisees, operators, and general managers about the challenges they face. One thing that continues to stand out is how much responsibility falls on the people managing daily operations. While restaurants have adopted technology to improve everything from scheduling and inventory management to hiring and employee communication, the effectiveness of these systems ultimately depends on how well they fit into the manager’s existing workflow. Hiring is a particularly good example. A manager may post a position, receive applications throughout the day, and then have to remember to log into a separate platform to review candidates. Meanwhile, they’re managing a busy lunch service, responding to employee questions, or handling an unexpected absence. By the time they return to the hiring process, valuable time may have passed, and promising candidates may have already pursued other opportunities. The challenge isn’t necessarily a lack of technology. It’s that many systems still require managers to actively seek out information rather than making relevant information easily accessible when it’s needed. Technology Should Reduce Work, Not Create More of It Restaurant managers are rarely sitting behind a desk throughout the day. They’re moving between the kitchen, dining room, and their teams, responding to operational demands as they arise. Their phones have naturally become an important part of how they communicate, coordinate schedules, and manage day-to-day responsibilities. Hiring technology should recognize this reality rather than expect managers to adopt an entirely different workflow. When a candidate applies for a position, that information shouldn’t remain unnoticed simply because a manager hasn’t had time to check a dashboard. Providing timely notifications can help managers stay informed about new applications and determine when action is required. The objective isn’t to encourage managers to spend more time on their phones, but to reduce the effort involved in staying connected to the hiring process. Beyond notifications, technology should help streamline the administrative responsibilities that often slow recruiting down. Organizing applications, screening candidates against job requirements, managing communication, and coordinating interviews are all areas where the right tools can make a meaningful difference. Instead of requiring managers to manually review every application and track each interaction, a well-designed system should help identify relevant candidates and make the next steps easier to manage. At Swob, this philosophy has influenced how we’ve approached restaurant hiring. By bringing job distribution, candidate management, and screening into one centralized system, while providing text notifications when candidates apply, our goal is to make recruiting more manageable for restaurant operators. Technology should support the hiring process by organizing information and reducing repetitive tasks, while leaving the final decisions in the hands of the people who understand their teams and businesses best.
